conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: UXCascade: Scalable Usability Testing with Simulated User Agents.
abstract: Simulated user agents are increasingly deployed in usability testing to support fast, iterative UX workflows, as they generate rich data such as action logs and think-aloud reasoning, but the unstructured nature of this output often obscures actionable insights. We present UXCascade, an interactive tool for extracting, aggregating, and presenting agent-generated usability feedback at scale. Our core contribution is a multi-level analysis workflow that (1) highlights patterns across persona traits, goals, and outcomes, (2) links agent reasoning to specific issues, and (3) supports actionable design improvements. UXCascade operationalizes this approach by listing agent goals, traits, and issues in a structured overview. Practitioners can explore detailed reasoning traces and annotated views, propose interface edits, and assess their impact across personas. This enables a top-down, exploration-driven analysis from patterns to concrete, actionable UX interventions. A user study with eight UX professionals demonstrates that UXCascade integrates into existing workflows, enabling iterative feedback during early-stage interface development.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: What If You Could Call Your Future Self? NicoCall as a Personalized Future-Self Video Call for Nicotine Cessation.
abstract: Interacting with one’s future self may support nicotine cessation, but effective design requires balancing trust, emotional impact, and user acceptance. We present NicoCall, a personalized future-self video call system that supports Hoped-for and Feared framings, grounded in Possible Selves theory. We ran a three-condition between-subjects experiment (N = 51) comparing the Hoped-for Self, Feared Self, and Control conditions on post-session Future Self-Continuity Questionnaire (FSCQ) scores, smoking urge, and smoking cessation self-efficacy. The findings suggest that NicoCall was associated with higher post-session FSCQ scores and self-efficacy, and with lower smoking urge overall. Hoped-for framing showed more consistent gains in FSCQ scores and self-efficacy, whereas framing differences in urge reduction remained directional. Qualitative findings further suggest that personal fit and social presence may shape uptake of future-self interaction, with identical visual and interactional elements interpreted differently across framing conditions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Declarative Dragging.
abstract: Drag-and-drop interactions realize the vision of direct manipulation, allowing objects to be manipulated in intuitive and responsive ways. However, implementing such interactions typically requires managing complex spatial, temporal, and visual behaviors. We present a higher-level alternative, declarative dragging (D2). D2 is model-driven: An interface author makes an element draggable by specifying which future model states should be accessible by dragging it. An engine speculatively renders these states to view trees, extracts the position of the dragged element in each of these renderings, and uses these to synthesize a drag-and-drop interaction, all without detailed work required by the interface author. To provide greater expressive range and customizability, D2 is composable: simple model-driven drag-and-drop behaviors can be combined to create more complex ones, and modifiers can layer features like floating, snapping, and transitions. To test D2, we built a prototype engine called Dragology. We demonstrate that Dragology’s model-driven primitives can concisely express a broad range of high-quality drag-and-drop interactions. Interviews with 13 interface developers suggest declarative dragging lowers the floor for building polished, varied drag-and-drop interactions – while surfacing barriers to learning and adoption.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Understanding the Role of AI-Enabled Live Tables in Scholarly Sensemaking.
abstract: AI-assisted tools are increasingly used to support information extraction and multi-document reading in research workflows. However, conventional conversational LLM interfaces often mismatch researchers’ specific needs, potentially inducing unnecessary cognitive load. To explore more effective interaction paradigms, we developed Lignin , an academic literature reading tool centered on tabular information representation and real-time AI querying. Building on existing table-based reading tools, Lignin combines dynamically configurable query columns, per-cell regeneration and editing, and source-level traceability. This design allows users to revise query dimensions as their questions evolve and supports cross-document comparison during scholarly sensemaking. A controlled experiment was conducted to examine the impact of this tool versus traditional AI interaction modes on cognitive activities during exploratory tasks in unfamiliar domains. Through observations and interviews, we identified instances in which participants appeared to benefit from particular design features, clarifying how different information formats and interaction styles influence such tasks. These findings offer valuable insights for the design of future AI-assisted reading tools and the optimization of AI-mediated research practices.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: XTick: Rendering Omnidirectional Hit-and-Hold Impact Feedback All Round a Controller by Integrating Impact and Pressing Force.
abstract: Impact feedback, with a sharp force increase and short duration, is common in VR. However, in some scenarios, force feedback consists of an impact force peak followed by sustained force with a smaller magnitude, extending the overall force application duration of such hit-and-hold impact force feedback, e.g., when swords press against each other, or when a shield resists propelled projectiles or falling rocks, which is critical but less discussed. Moreover, rendering impact at the position and direction corresponding to VR scenarios is also crucial. We propose a controller, XTick, to render omnidirectional short-duration instant impact and long-duration hit-and-hold impact feedback all round the controller by integrating impact and pressing force. It enables omnidirectional pressing force and integrates it with impact at various positions and directions to render impact in any duration. To achieve seamless integration, this work investigated two critical factors: force magnitude alignment between impact and pressing force in a feedback integration study, and the transition between initial impact and sustained force states in an impact extension study. Based on the results and guidelines, a VR study was conducted to verify that the integrated feedback from XTick enhances VR experiences and show some applications.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: OmniTex: Omnidirectional Haptic Rendering of Surface Texture on VR Handheld Controller using 3-DOF Motion Mechanism.
abstract: Extensive research has explored haptic rendering of surface textures in virtual reality (VR). However, it is still challenging to provide realistic texture-based haptic feedback that aligns with users’ fingertip motion in VR. We present OmniTex, a handheld haptic device that enables continuous omnidirectional texture rendering in VR. OmniTex integrates a 2 DoF rotational mechanism to support fingertip-aligned motion and deliver directional shear feedback, together with a linear translation mechanism for dynamic texture switching. Technical evaluation revealed low latency averaging around 250ms with our system for texture switching and motion synchronization. Our user studies further demonstrated the effectiveness of our design in improving user-perceived visual–tactile congruence in VR with different finger movements and different types of virtual textures, and our system offered significantly better sense of realism in VR compared with controller-based vibration, achieving performance comparable to that of real-surface proxy interaction.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ITO: Real-time Browser Tab Orchestration Through Intent Detection.
abstract: People routinely interleave activities while browsing the web, often simultaneously and with overlapping boundaries. Yet organizational primitives in modern browsers treat every tab uniformly, offering no structural awareness of which items serve which purpose. While task-based organization approaches exist, they typically require users to manually organize or invoke reorganization features, and quickly fall out of sync as user intents evolve. To address this, we present Ito, a mixed-initiative approach that infers user intent in real time and organizes browsing activities into dynamic collections called Flows. Ito continuously reads unfolding user context, determines moment-to-moment focus, and creates, restructures, hibernates, and awakens Flows in real time while preserving user control through a mixed-initiative loop of proposals and corrections. In a controlled lab study (N=12) and a two-week field study (N=11), results suggest that Ito’s intent-driven Flows aligned more closely with participants’ mental models, facilitated task switching and navigation more effectively, and reduced management burden without loss of perceived control.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CinemaWorld: Generative Augmented Reality with LLMs and 3D Scene Generation for Movie Augmentation.
abstract: We introduce CinemaWorld, a generative augmented reality system that augments the viewer’s physical surroundings with automatically generated mixed reality 3D content extracted from and synchronized with 2D movie scenes. Our system preprocesses films to extract key features using multimodal large language models (LLMs), generates dynamic 3D augmentations with generative AI, and embeds them spatially into the viewer’s physical environment on the Meta Quest 3. To identify key augmentation techniques for CinemaWorld, we conducted an elicitation study with eight film students, which led us to identify several key augmentation types, including particle effects, surrounding objects, textural overlays, character-driven augmentation, and lighting effects. We evaluated our system through a technical evaluation (N=100 video clips), a user evaluation (comparison study: N=12 and in-the-wild study: N=8), and expert interviews with film creators (N=8). Results indicate that CinemaWorld enhances immersion and enjoyment, suggesting its potential to enrich the film-viewing experience.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: AeroPixels: Repurposing Ubiquitous Displays as Imperceptible Schlieren Light Sources for Airflow Interaction.
abstract: Airflow is an invisible yet ubiquitous phenomenon in everyday environments, encoding rich information about human activities and environmental conditions such as exhalation, thermal convection, and ventilation. We present AeroPixels, a method that leverages ubiquitous display surfaces as an airflow sensing infrastructure. AeroPixels embeds the source grid pattern required for focusing schlieren imaging, an optical technique that visualizes airflow through light refraction, into displayed visual content and perceptually hides it via alternating complementary, high-frame-rate frames, allowing users to perceive only the intended imagery. A schlieren camera synchronized with the display refresh captures each complementary frame independently and reconstructs airflow information. We address key challenges in display-based sensing, including geometric misalignment between the embedded source grid pattern and the sensing camera, as well as content-dependent noise, enabling robust schlieren imaging under non-ideal conditions such as projection mapping environments. We build a prototype system and demonstrate stable airflow visualization on projected surfaces while preserving the intended visual content for human observers. Finally, we present three representative projection modes for human-computer interaction enabled by AeroPixels, including exhalation visualization, breath-based input, education, and entertainment.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Projective Walls, Floors, and Windows: Aligned Plane Interactions for Interior Architectural Design in VR.

title: Great Grave: Modeling Versioned Context Units for Longitudinal LLM Interaction.
abstract: Researchers use LLM chat for sustained intellectual work across long conversations—formulating problems, designing methods, and iterating on ideas. The resulting chat logs function as documents co-authored by the researcher and the model. Yet their linear structure turns them into a rich but practically unusable repository, a “great grave” where valuable decisions and rationale are buried in ever-growing scrolls of text. We present Great Grave, a system that transforms LLM chat logs into Research Workflow Graphs. Our approach segments conversations into intent-driven Context Units, groups them into decision-tracked Work Units, and extracts typed relations to form a navigable graph. An overlay interface provides a List View for hierarchical retrieval and a Graph View for relational exploration. A within-subjects study (N = 12) showed that the overlay significantly improved performance on research comprehension tasks, with the largest gains in tasks requiring cross-temporal comparison and evolutionary reconstruction. While techniques such as context windows and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) help models leverage history, Great Grave enables users to do the same.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: HALO: Interactive Co-abductive Reasoning in Hypothesis Generation for Scientific Discovery.
abstract: Scientific discovery is essential yet inefficient, primarily because generating hypotheses within a vast search space hinders breakthroughs. While current AI systems assist in generating new hypothesis candidates, they lack interactive support for the reasoning process by which users develop these outputs into promising hypotheses, resulting in surface-level hypotheses. To address this issue, we present a co-abduction, a human-AI collaborative framework for abductive reasoning in scientific hypothesis generation. To operationalize co-abduction, we build HALO, a human–AI collaborative system for molecular hypothesis generation in drug discovery, enabling improved candidate clustering, strategy identification, and multi-strategy synthesis. In expert studies involving 10 medicinal chemists, HALO significantly facilitated abductive reasoning for hypothesis generation—efficient candidate observation, systematic strategy identification, and coherent multi-strategy composition—and enabled participants to produce higher-quality, more diverse candidate molecules.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SwapSense: Reusable Vision-Based Contact Force Sensing Across Swappable Passive Haptic Modules.
abstract: The haptic qualities of physical interfaces—such as key-click sensations and stylus-tip stiffness—strongly shape user experience beyond functional performance. Prior work has explored reconfigurable passive structures to diversify such haptic experiences, but existing solutions typically sacrifice rich sensing capabilities or require dedicated sensing modules for each configuration. In this paper, we present SwapSense, a modular vision-based haptic I/O framework that physically decouples a shared sensing module from interchangeable haptic augmentation modules. A camera captures sequential deformation of a shared sensing substrate, and an encoder–decoder network estimates contact forces, while each attached augmentation module independently modulates force–displacement characteristics. Our results show that a model trained for pressing force estimation can generalize across users and support effective adaptation to previously unseen augmentation components. Across leave-one-augmentation-out evaluations, adaptation to unseen target components required at most 25% of target-component data, with fine-tuning completed within 15 minutes. A complementary perceptual study further shows that the five haptic augmentations span a perceptually diverse two-dimensional perceptual space. Together, these results demonstrate that SwapSense enables reusable contact force sensing and perceptually expressive passive haptic reconfiguration within a single framework.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ArtScape: Detecting, Characterizing, and Interactively Exploring Urban Art at Scale Using Vision Language Models.
abstract: Urban art brings cultural expression, community identity, and aesthetic enrichment to cities. Currently, there are no systematic ways of exploring urban art at scale. We introduce ArtScape, a VLM-based interactive tool that lets users view, search, filter, and tour four categories of art (murals, mosaics, sculptures, graffiti). To comprehensively and automatically detect urban artwork throughout a region, we designed a custom five-stage pipeline that uses VLMs to detect and describe urban artwork within 360° panoramic Street View images, achieving a micro-F1 of 0.83 on an urban art dataset we labeled. ArtScape categorizes, describes, and scores the reachability and interestingness of each artwork while deduplicating based on proximity and similarity. We evaluated this tool with 12 participants spanning urban planners, artists, sighted users, and blind and low vision users. Our findings show that ArtScape’s at-scale AI artwork curation enables granular and aggregate urban art discovery, thereby helping people learn about their communities and city-wide trends, motivating in-person urban exploration, and expanding perceptions of what constitutes urban art.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PartInteractor: Intent-Driven Part-Aware 3D Authoring for Continuous Co-Creation in XR.
abstract: As Extended Reality (XR) evolves into an immersive computing medium, interactive 3D authoring becomes essential for creative and functional workflows. However, existing generative XR systems produce monolithic outputs lacking explicit semantic structure, limiting post-generation control. We introduce PartInteractor, a representation-to-interaction framework that investigates how semantic part hierarchies can be incorporated into generative XR authoring, and exposed as first-class, directly manipulable units, turning one-shot prompt-to-object generation into continuous component-level co-creation. PartInteractor supports speech, sketch, and image inputs, integrating an LLM interpreter with a retrieval-generation strategy to scaffold user intent prior to 3D generation. Instead of producing monolithic objects, our system generates semantically decomposed 3D assets with explicit part hierarchies, enabling rich component-level interaction over object structure and composition. Our evaluations suggest that part-aware representation increases post-generation control and reduces reliance on whole-object regeneration, while intent scaffolding mitigates ambiguity and improves intent-result alignment, together supporting more expressive and controllable human-AI co-creation workflows. These results highlight part-aware representation and intent scaffolding as promising design considerations for future generative XR authoring systems.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: InvisiSpeech: Making Silent Speech Invisible through a Miniature Intraoral Sensor.
abstract: Silent speech promises private interaction, but existing implementations often rely on visible sensors or conspicuous articulation, which limits their discretion in everyday use. We present InvisiSpeech, an intraoral interface that remains hidden from outside view and supports silent speech input with minimal lip movement and without drawing visual attention. Our custom flex-PCB device is housed in a biocompatible SLA-printed dental brace and attaches around the back molar. This mount couples a voice-pickup sensor to the tooth for input sensing, which our embedded microcontroller transfers via Bluetooth. Our evaluation with 15 participants shows that InvisiSpeech achieves up to 91.5% recognition accuracy on 50 sentence-level commands and maintains robustness in noisy environments. Participants also reported high wearability and perceived social acceptance, highlighting the practicality of our approach for daily use. We demonstrate three applications of our system: hands-free human–AI interaction in public, discreet interaction in a quiet public place, and subtle communication in a privacy-sensitive context. Our results establish invisible silent speech as a practical interaction paradigm for real-world use outside controlled settings.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TeethMark: Enabling Tongue-Tooth Interaction with Capacitive Sensing and Electrotactile Feedback using an Intraoral Wearable.
abstract: We present TeethMark, an intraoral interface that enables tongue–tooth interaction by leveraging the tongue as the active medium for gesture input and electro-tactile feedback, while utilizing teeth as positional cues for localization. By applying a flexible PCB on a 3D-printed brace, TeethMark can recognize tapping, sliding, and area-touch gestures, and deliver two forms of electrotactile feedback: co-located feedback when the tongue touches the inner side of the teeth, and always-available feedback on the lip-facing side. With our design tool, users can customize and generate their own flexible PCB layouts, selecting interaction locations at the level of individual teeth. We conducted a formative study examining the physical comfort and social acceptability of tongue gestures across different tooth locations. The validation study evaluates the perception of electrotactile feedback and the accuracy of tongue–tooth gesture recognition. Our results indicate that TeethMark provides a promising modality for discreet, hands-free interaction. We further demonstrate its versatility through a set of applications, including language education, VR sensory sharing, gamified myofunctional therapy, and fabrication tool support.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: EIJaw: Non-Invasive Intraoral User Interface with Electrical Impedance Sensing.
abstract: Oral interfaces provide an alternative to conventional input methods for hands-free interaction in assistive and multitasking scenarios, yet existing solutions are limited by lacking capability of detecting internal muscle movements or safety risks from intraoral electronics. Inspired by electrical impedance (EI) tomography, we introduce EIJaw, a non-invasive prototype that characterizes intraoral movements through impedance variations in suprahyoid muscles. We demonstrate its effectiveness through experiments with six participants performing kana pronunciation, silent pronunciation, and tongue movement tasks, achieving feasible classification of diverse intraoral movements via deep learning. By eliminating the need for electronics inside the mouth while maintaining feasible recognition accuracy, EIJaw offers a proof of concept for future oral interface applications with electrical impedance measurement technology.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Eliciting Empathetic Expression Through Robot-Initiated Touch in Companion Scenarios.
abstract: Companion robots are becoming increasingly integrated into everyday life, making the ability to express empathy a critical aspect of their design. However, prior research has focused primarily on verbal and visual cues, leaving robot-initiated touch largely underexplored. To address this gap, we first conducted a pilot study to identify six representative robots whose proactive touch was most acceptable across three morphology types (Human-like, Animal-like, and Machine-like). We then conducted an elicitation study to examine users’ expectations for robot-initiated touch across four emotional states (Happy, Depressed, Tense, and Relaxed). The results showed that both emotional states and robot morphology shaped preferred touch locations and touch behaviors, yielding a set of 24 user-preferred touch gestures. Finally, a Wizard-of-Oz study in a virtual environment demonstrated that a balanced subset of these gestures effectively conveyed empathic intent and improved both users’ affective states and their perceptions of the robots. These findings provide design implications for robot-initiated touch in future companion robots.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Map2Video: Guiding Real-World-Grounded AI Video Generation.
abstract: AI video generation lowers barriers to video creation, but existing tools provide limited support for grounding content in real-world locations, restricting their use in applications such as film previsualization and scenario generation. In practice, users rely on verbose textual descriptions or reference images using on-site photos or street view imagery (SVI), which are cumbersome and unreliable across shots. Our formative study with five filmmakers revealed challenges in shot composition, character motion, and camera control when using SVI with an image-to-video tool. We present Map2Video, a system for guiding SVI-grounded AI video generation through map-based character trajectory annotation and direct manipulation of cameras and character masks defined in geodetic coordinates and projected onto panoramic screen coordinates. In an evaluation with twelve filmmakers, Map2Video provided stronger controllability for both scene replication and open-ended creative exploration, reduced cognitive effort, and improved spatial consistency across multiple shots compared to an image-to-video baseline.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Cardinal Pressure Pulses Rendered by a Wristband Can Elicit Phantom Directional Cues.
abstract: Extended reality systems are moving toward camera-based hand tracking, abandoning controllers and the helpful haptic feedback they commonly provide. While many wrist-worn devices can output vibrations, pressure pulse cues offer a promising alternative: they operate silently and deliver comfortable, focal percepts distinct from the buzzing of vibrotactile motors. We present SuperCUTE, a 15-gram wristband with four soft cutaneous electrohydraulic actuators that apply pressure at cardinal wrist positions. Phantom tactile sensations, created by co-activating adjacent actuators, can expand the directional vocabulary of sparse haptic arrays beyond their physical sites. Building on this idea, we characterize the directional cueing capabilities of SuperCUTE in a study with twenty participants. Single-actuator 2-Hz pressure pulses were localized with high precision (∼ 71% of responses within ± 22.5° of the target), adjacent pairs usually produced phantom percepts at intermediate directions, and intensity imbalance steered perceived direction toward the stronger actuator, expanding the wristband’s four actuators into sixteen directional cues spanning 360°. During haptic-only VR guidance, hand movement directions matched cue geometry across all cue types. Demonstrations of closed-loop haptic guidance and orbiting pressure animations illustrate how spatially distributed pressure pulse cues can enrich extended reality interactions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CLOAK: A Privacy-Preserving Assistant for Online Social Media Users.
abstract: Many people share personal details on platforms like Reddit under the assumption that a pseudonymous account keeps their identity safe. They do not realize that a profession mentioned in one subreddit, a hobby in another, and a neighborhood in a third can be pieced together to narrow down exactly who they are. Large language models have made this kind of cross-post profiling easy to do at scale. Yet existing tools offer little help: PII scanners catch names and emails but miss contextual cues, and even LLM-based privacy systems analyze only the current post in isolation, missing the cross-post combinations that actually compromise anonymity. We present CLOAK, a system that examines a user’s full posting history alongside their draft comment and shows them the identification risk before they post. A pipeline of four LLM agents extracts a structured attribute profile from prior posts, identifies cross-post interactions that narrow the anonymity set, ranks risky phrases, and suggests minimal edits that preserve the user’s intent. CLOAK is designed as an awareness tool for informed self-disclosure: rather than blocking or redacting content, it helps users understand the trade-offs and decide for themselves. In a technical evaluation on 368 Reddit profiles, CLOAK detected cross-post tipping points in 77% of cases while the status quo baseline detected none. In a user study (N = 20), CLOAK was unanimously selected as the most helpful tool (trust: 6.5/7 vs. 1.5/7 for PII scanning), and every participant reported changed posting behavior.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: GuitarFins: Skillful Input Triggering with a Guitar Pick.
abstract: Having a guitar strapped on inevitably restricts physical movement when it comes to using digital interfaces (e.g., via mouse and keyboard) or adjusting equipment settings in between. Furthermore, guitarists typically use a guitar pick, which is often an additional hindrance—the pick often needs to be tucked or put down whenever having to operate an interface, which incurs additional context switching costs. However, we believe that the guitar pick can be turned from a hindrance into an opportunity by utilizing the guitarists’ dexterity with a pick for fast and convenient user input. We introduce GuitarFins—physical input elements, with which the pick becomes the end-effector for physical user input. To test the performance and subjective experience of using guitar-embedded input while holding a pick, we conducted a user study with 16 guitarists for which we augmented two guitars—one with GuitarFins and one with buttons. We found a variety of nuanced differences in terms of performance and individual preferences.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Explorable Proofs: Making Written Proofs Explorable by Grounding Them in Formal Representations.
abstract: LLM-generated explanations can make technical content more accessible, but there is a ceiling on what they can support interactively. Because LLM outputs are static text, they cannot be executed, tinkered with, or stepped through. In this paper, we explore how grounding explanations in a formalized representation enables interactive affordances beyond what static text supports. We instantiate this idea for mathematical proof comprehension in explorable proofs, an approach that uses LLMs to translate a theorem and its written proof into Lean, a programming language for machine-checked proofs, and links the written proof with the Lean code. Readers can work through the proof at a step-level granularity, test custom examples or counterexamples, and trace the logical dependencies bridging between steps. Each worked-out step is produced by executing the Lean proof on an example and extracting its intermediate state. A user study (n = 16) shows potential advantages of this approach: in a proof-understanding task, participants who used the explorability features wrote proof descriptions that an instructor preferred over those written with a proof-and-chatbot baseline, and gave more correct and more detailed answers to proof comprehension questions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Attribution Gradients: Incrementally Unfolding Citations for Critical Examination of Attributed AI Answers.

title: LitPivot: Developing Well-Situated Research Ideas Through Dynamic Contextualization and Critique within the Literature Landscape.
abstract: Developing a novel research idea is hard. It must be distinct enough from prior work to claim a contribution while also building on it. This requires iteratively reviewing literature and refining an idea based on what a researcher reads; yet when an idea changes, the literature that matters often changes with it. Most tools offer limited support for this interplay: literature tools help researchers understand a fixed body of work, while ideation tools evaluate ideas against a static, pre-curated set of papers. We introduce literature-initiated pivots, a mechanism where engagement with literature prompts revision to a developing idea, and where that revision changes which literature is relevant. We operationalize this in LitPivot, where researchers concurrently draft and vet an idea. LitPivot dynamically retrieves clusters of papers relevant to a selected part of the idea and proposes literature-informed critiques for how to revise it. A user study (n = 17) shows researchers produced ideas rated by experts as better grounded, perceived their ideas as more novel and useful, and reported stronger understanding of the literature space. An open-ended study (n = 5) reveals how researchers use LitPivot to iteratively evolve their own ideas.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Inertia in Your Hand: Rendering Virtual Tool Dynamics via In-Hand Cutaneous Deformation.
abstract: We present the Inertia Handle, a handheld haptic device that renders virtual tool dynamics through in-hand cutaneous deformation. The device reproduces relative motion between the handle and the hand when users swing virtual tools with different lengths, weights, and mass distributions. We model hand-tool coupling as an axis-specific rotational spring-damper system and update its parameters from the measured grip force. Through three studies, we evaluate (1) hand-tool rotational impedance, (2) perception of virtual tool direction and length, and (3) haptic experience in VR tool-use scenarios. Results show that stiffness and damping increased across grip force levels and differed across axes. Users identified virtual tool direction across multiple directions and discriminated rod length from in-hand cutaneous cues. In VR scenarios, the device improved haptic experience over a commercial VR controller, and tool-specific rendering further improved the realism and visual-haptic congruence of tool use. These findings show that in-hand cutaneous deformation can render virtual tool dynamics in VR without external weights or large actuators.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PÅCKER: Making Large Laser-Cut Objects Easy-to-Store and Transport.
abstract: We present PÅCKER, a software tool that makes large, laser-cut 3D objects efficient to pack and ship. Inspired by modern flat-pack furniture, PÅCKER achieves this by decomposing 3D models into multiple 3D components. Components are pre-assembled at the vendor’s site, shipped efficiently (since components tend to be convex, they pack well), and post-assembled IKEA-style at the receiver’s site. PÅCKER users decompose models using our custom split tool, which requires them to specify only where to split the model; the tool then automatically selects the most suitable split plane and connector type. Models componentized using PÅCKER are robust: in our technical evaluation, they withstood 94Nm+ of torque. In our user study, participants assembled decomposed chair models about 3.6x faster than the control group and rated them as requiring less demand to assemble.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ProConte: Supporting Progressive Authoring of Anime Storyboards through Partial and Exceptional Representations.
abstract: Creative practice is rarely fully formal. Even in highly structured production settings, professionals routinely rely on incomplete entries, deferred decisions, and exceptions to standard formats in order to think, explore, and communicate. In storyboard authoring, such deviations are not edge cases but part of the work itself. We present ProConte, a user interface for Japanese animation (anime) storyboarding that accommodates partialness and exceptions through a malleable substrate and a set of coordinated interfaces. Developed in close collaboration with a professional anime director, ProConte supports unspecified timings, exceptionally sized frames for expressive camera work, and unordered free-canvas frames for tentative externalization. The director used ProConte to author the complete storyboard for a 25-minute television anime episode, and we conducted six two-hour lecture sessions in which he created storyboards while explaining his process aloud. Together, the episode production and lecture sessions provided complementary qualitative evidence: the former situated ProConte in real-world production, while the latter made the director’s authoring process more inspectable. These materials showed that, in this case, our design supported progressive authoring in practice: ideas could be externalized before they were fully specified, revisited later, and developed across multiple semantically distinct stages without premature commitment to a formal structure.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Maru: Information Architecture as a Shared Language for Generating Aligned and Persistent User Interfaces.
abstract: Generative user interfaces (GenUIs) promise on-demand components tailored to users’ needs. As users iterate on information tasks, they construct personal structures over information they encounter—how items are grouped, what gets prioritized, and what terms mean in their context. Yet, current systems leave these structural decisions to the model at each generation, ignoring the structural logic users have established. Without a persistent representational structure shared between user and system, GenUIs have no basis to remain aligned with what users have established. We draw on Information Architecture (IA), a design practice for organizing and structuring information, as a shared language to bridge user-constructed structure and system generation. We present a framework identifying four IA elements—partition, hierarchy, order, and vocabulary—and characterize how each maps to concrete UI generation decisions. We instantiate this framework in Maru, a conversational system that captures user prompts and interactions as IA preferences, persisting as rules both user and system draw on across generations. A user study revealed that IA persistence kept generated UIs aligned as sessions progressed, while alignment without it degraded, with diverse patterns emerging across users and contexts, pointing to the value of IA persistence in aligning GenUI to individual needs.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: GazeTune: Facilitating Precise Gaze-Driven Interactions with Cascaded Touch Input.
abstract: Eye gaze has become an essential input for spatial computing, but its coarse targeting and saccadic nature limit precision and complicate continuous interactions such as dragging, especially under user motion. Gaze+pinch has also become standard in XR for its convenience, yet mid-air gestures remain imprecise, fatiguing, and socially unacceptable. These limitations underscore the need for an approach that preserves the speed of gaze while enabling stable, fine control. We present GazeTune, a cascaded multimodal interaction technique combining gaze and touch to refine gaze-based selection and manipulation. Touch serves as a refinement channel within gaze pointing, allowing precise cursor and target control. Our work investigates how gaze-and-touch enhances dragging and mitigates Motion-Induced instability. In a study (N=20), we compared GazeTune against gaze-only and gaze-pinch methods in 2D dragging. Results show that GazeTune achieves significantly lower error with comparable execution time, validating its effectiveness and balanced trade-off between time and accuracy.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Co-opting Mobile Device Cellular RF Front Ends for HCI Sensing.
abstract: Modern smartphones contain sophisticated cellular modems that can tune their antennas. We show how this latent internal capability, intended to minimize power consumption while maximizing antenna performance, can be co-opted as a sensing capability in already ubiquitous mobile devices. For example, we can sense electromagnetic loading from a user’s hand, surrounding objects, and nearby materials, enabling diverse applications such as detecting grip pose, worn device placement, and passive interactive widgets. As a proof of concept, we selected five example use cases from the HCI literature, created with different and specialized sensors, and re-implemented them with a commercial off-the-shelf smartphone. We use these to evaluate sensing performance, comparing to prior work, and the results underscore the promise and generalizability of smartphone RF hardware as a future sensing modality.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Object-Agent Twins (OATs): Expressive Micro-Agent Avatars for Inanimate Everyday Objects.
abstract: We introduce Object-Agent Twins (OATs), a toolkit for creating Tamagotchi-like companions for inanimate everyday objects. OATs allow non-expert users to easily author small personality-bearing agents tied to real-world artifacts such as a tea kettle, pet bowls, and a trash can. These OATs act as expressive proxies for physical objects, using real-time sensed data to drive simple needs, moods, and behaviors. In contrast to conventional smart-object interfaces that expose raw status and data, OATs render object state through character, making everyday infrastructure more socially legible and emotionally engaging. Through deployments, we show how this approach enables users to transform ordinary things in their lives from passive infrastructure into lightweight companions that invite attention, interpretation, and care.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Interactively Teaching Collaborative Physical Tasks to Generative AI with Narrated Demonstrations.
abstract: Enabling users to teach computers how to perform physical tasks is a long-standing goal in HCI. Prior work has explored learning from demonstration, but demonstrations often underspecify intent. Advances in generative AI enable a combination of demonstration and verbal narration to disambiguate intent. However, it remains largely unexplored how to design interfaces that leverage such narrated demonstrations to teach collaborative physical tasks. To probe this design space, we present a prototype system, Apprento, that models physical tasks as programs via generative AI with three integrated interfaces: (1) a teaching interface for providing narrated demonstrations in mixed reality, (2) an inspection interface for visualizing generated programs as decision-flow diagrams and program executions, and (3) a correction interface for iteratively refining generated programs. Across these interfaces, narrated demonstrations serve as a communication modality between users and the system. In a study with 20 participants teaching soccer skills, we identify differing user expectations around authoring and teaching collaborative tasks, as well as key design tensions between task complexity and program interpretability, and between program expressivity and accuracy. We discuss implications for designing future systems that support symbolic modeling of collaborative physical tasks through narrated demonstrations.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CaseSense: Mapping the Legal Case Landscape with Multi-Dimensional Visual Exploration.
abstract: Legal case research requires combining facts, legal principles, and timelines into persuasive arguments. Yet existing retrieval tools return one-dimensional ranked lists, collapsing this structure into a single relevance score. A formative study with five lawyers confirmed this flat output leads to missed cases, temporal gaps, and fragmented reasoning. We present CaseSense, a visual analytics system for multi-dimensional exploration via tri-axial mapping with dynamic weighting, anchor-based navigation, and purpose-constrained view projections. A within-subjects study with 16 legal professionals compared CaseSense against conventional workflows. CaseSense achieved complete key-case discovery in the Fact Synthesis task, with the largest gains in organization and connection identification. Participants adopted task-matched interaction strategies without instructions. These findings suggest encoding domain reasoning dimensions as manipulable spatial axes supports expert sensemaking, while separating spatial organization from AI-generated content preserves verification behavior.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: AgentLens: Adaptive Visual Modalities for Human-Agent Interaction in Mobile GUI Agents.
abstract: Mobile GUI agents can automate smartphone tasks by interacting directly with app interfaces, but how they should communicate with users during execution remains underexplored. Existing systems rely on two extremes: foreground execution, which maximizes transparency but prevents multitasking, and background execution, which supports multitasking but provides little visual awareness. Through iterative formative studies, we found that users prefer a hybrid model with minimally invasive, just-in-time visual interaction, but the most effective visualization modality depends on the task. Motivated by this, we present AgentLens, a mobile GUI agent that adaptively uses three visual modalities during human–agent interaction: Full UI, Partial UI, and GenUI. AgentLens extends a standard mobile agent with adaptive communication actions and uses Virtual Display to enable background execution with selective visual overlays. In a controlled study with 21 participants, AgentLens was preferred by 85.7% of participants and achieved the highest usability (1.94 Overall PSSUQ; lower is better) and adoption intent (6.43/7).
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Democratizing Extensive Reading by Tailoring Web Content.
abstract: Extensive reading helps foreign language learners build proficiency through large amounts of interesting, level-appropriate text. However, providing enough material matched to learners’ interests and evolving proficiency is resource-intensive and difficult to sustain. To address this challenge, we present Adapt-ER, a browser extension that leverages the web to support scalable self-selected reading by adapting pages in place to each learner’s vocabulary profile. Adapt-ER estimates lexical proficiency, tailors web content in real time, and supports lightweight profile refinement through click-based interactive learner feedback during reading. To make adaptation practical during live browsing, we compare LLM-based strategies and develop a hybrid pipeline that balances lexical difficulty control, semantic preservation, latency, and cost. In a within-subject study, Adapt-ER increased reading speed, reduced the need for dictionary and translation support during reading, and improved self-reported engagement. Our findings suggest that in-place adaptation of self-selected web text can make web reading better suited to sustained extensive reading.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CineHaptic: Context-Aware Real-Time Audiovisual-to-Haptic Rendering System for In-Vehicle 4D Cinematic Experiences.
abstract: Haptic feedback significantly enriches cinematic experiences, but existing manual authoring and offline generation methods lack the scalability required for rapidly growing streaming media libraries. To address this, we present CineHaptic, a real-time system that automatically generates haptic effects for action-oriented cinematic content by estimating event salience and location for immersive in-vehicle 4D experiences. For each sound event, the system classifies its semantic salience into a four-level hierarchy, determining the necessity and intensity of haptic actuation. Concurrently, a cross-modal audiovisual analysis module estimates the sound’s spatial origin in the scene. CineHaptic then seamlessly synthesizes this semantic and spatial data into coherent spatiotemporal patterns, delivered through a custom six-actuator haptic seat. System-level evaluations confirm strict adherence to real-time processing and multisensory synchrony requirements over full-length cinematic content. Furthermore, an in-car user study shows that haptic feedback integrating audio salience, spatial location, and temporal dynamics significantly enhances user immersion and preference compared to baseline methods. Ultimately, our system provides a fully automated pipeline for multisensory rendering, tailored for next-generation in-car entertainment.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Neighborhood: Dynamic Spatial Alignment for Traversable Telepresence Across Remote Spaces.
abstract: We propose Neighborhood, a mixed reality (MR) telepresence system that allows users to experience an illusion of walking between local and remote spaces as if they are physically connected. Prior studies transmit either the avatar or the space alone to the remote space. Works that transmit both limit either remote space’s visibility or traversability to specific areas. Our work builds upon prior works by transmitting both the avatar and the space, while also supporting full visibility and traversability of local and remote spaces with user’s activities grounded with their real furniture and objects, distinct from VR traversal. Our system begins with users moving to the specific area they wish to connect. Using the chosen spaces, the optimization function aligns them to initiate Walking In Mode, visualizing a traversable area with remote spaces augmented. If users wish to move to a different area, the system transits to Panning Mode. Here, the moving user’s avatar appears stationary while the background shifts from the observing user’s perspective. We quantitatively measure metrics including the size of the neighborhood and ablate each term to evaluate the optimization function across diverse spatial configurations. We also conducted an exploratory user study with 21 participants, showing that traversing within Neighborhood evokes a compelling sense of real spatial adjoin.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Generating Personalized Games with Sensing Data to Support Self-Reported Data Collection.
abstract: Collecting in-situ behavioral data to support research studies often involves prompting repeated ecological momentary assessments (EMAs) on smartphones and wearables. Sustained engagement, however, remains a major challenge because study participants often experience survey fatigue and declining motivation over time. To address this challenge, we introduce Personalized Adaptive Games for Engagement (PAGE): a novel LLM-powered approach that integrates data collection with a personalized game experience. PAGE uses a participant’s previously collected data to dynamically generate personalized puzzles, embedding behavioral data collection within engaging gameplay. We deployed a prototype using a variant of a word wheel puzzle game in a two-week feasibility study (N=15); while participants responded to EMAs in both weeks of the study, they also received sensor-based personalized puzzles in one of those weeks. We found that most participants (80%) preferred the week with personalized puzzles. Participants also contributed richer EMA data (72 additional unique contextual tags) and 1,188 additional uncompensated responses via a feasible in-game data collection channel during the puzzle week. We discuss design guidelines for developing context-aware personalized games to support engagement, potentially for use in longitudinal studies.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Contexty: Capturing and Organizing In-situ Thoughts for Context-Aware AI Support.
abstract: During complex knowledge work, people engage in iterative sensemaking: interpreting information, connecting ideas, and refining their understanding. Yet in current human–AI collaboration, these cognitive processes are difficult to share and organize for AI. They arise in situ and are rarely captured without interrupting the task, and even when expressed, remain scattered or reduced to system-generated summaries that fail to reflect users’ cognitive processes. We address this challenge by enabling AI context that is grounded in users’ cognitive traces and can be directly inspected and revised by the user. We first explore this through a probe system that supports in-situ snippet memoing, allowing users to easily share their cognitive moves. Our study (N=10) highlights the value of capturing such context and the challenge of organizing it once accumulated. We then present Contexty, which supports users in inspecting and refining these contexts to better reflect their understanding of the task. Our evaluation (N=12) showed that Contexty improved task awareness, thought structuring, and users’ sense of authorship and control, with participants preferring snippet-grounded AI responses over non-grounded ones (78.1%). We discuss how capturing and organizing users’ cognitive context enables AI as a context-aware collaborator while preserving user agency.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: DOBI: Dynamic Opportunistic Body Input via Spare Joint Recruitment for Hands-Free XR.
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) systems are often most useful when users are engaged in ongoing physical tasks, yet current interaction techniques still largely assume the hands are available. We present opportunistic body input, an interaction paradigm that redirects continuous XR control to whichever available body region remains free in the moment. To investigate how users naturally coordinate these spare-body movements, we conducted an elicitation study across six hand-busy scenarios. We found that while users’ preferred spare body regions shift dynamically based on physical constraints, the resulting spontaneous movements share a consistent, low-dimensional kinematic structure organized around a dominant principal axis. Building on these findings, we present DOBI (Dynamic Opportunistic Body Input), a real-time XR technique that uses gaze to target a UI element, a brief trigger gesture to identify the recruited spare body region, and the region’s subsequent motion to drive continuous 1D control. A 1D Fitts’ law study establishes the baseline motor performance of this paradigm across four distinct body regions, achieving throughputs up to 2.62 bits/s with an overall 5.0% error rate, and a dual-task usability study shows that DOBI supports reliable, low-effort control (SUS = 84.2) while users remain engaged in realistic hand-busy activities.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Print&Fold: Printing and Folding Shape-accurate 3D Models.
abstract: This paper introduces Print&Fold, a tool to allow FDM 3D printing of complex models with less time and material while preserving shape accuracy. Key to this work is a folding algorithm that planarizes foldable faces internal to the 3D model. While folding techniques typically discretize a target model’s surface, thereby fabricating low fidelity counterparts, our method preserves the surface features in the physical print. Our design tool allows users to unfold 3D models to be FDM-printed flat before manually folding these into their target shapes. We showcase a variety of applications and evaluate the material and time savings across a range of 3D models.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: HAPTCHA: Eyes-Free Haptic CAPTCHA in Mobile Environments: Design Principle, Security Evaluation, and User Experience.
abstract: Traditional visual CAPTCHAs face dual challenges: increasing vulnerability to automated solvers and maintaining usability without imposing excessive visual burden. We propose Haptic CAPTCHA (HAPTCHA), an eyes-free human-verification framework that leverages smartphone vibration as the primary information channel. HAPTCHA grounds security in a human closed-loop sensorimotor process that is inherently difficult for automated agents to emulate. We instantiate this framework through two complementary designs: tiltHAPTCHA, an efficiency-oriented spatial search task, and rhythmHAPTCHA, a robustness-oriented temporal reproduction task. Our security analysis against sophisticated imitation-learning bots shows that HAPTCHA’s structured interaction traces provide a robust signal for discrimination, achieving up to 100% bot rejection rate in unseen attack scenarios. The usability evaluation across sitting, walking, and fast-walking scenarios demonstrates that HAPTCHA maintains high solvability (e.g., 96.7% success rate for tiltHAPTCHA while sitting) and offers superior usability with significantly lower cognitive workload than a visual reCAPTCHA mockup. These findings position HAPTCHA as an explicit haptic challenge layer that complements passive, risk-based verification by moving challenge information beyond the screen.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Precise Duration Control for Video Editing via LLM Scoring and Constrained Optimization.
abstract: Editing videos calls for satisfying two fundamentally different kinds of requirements simultaneously. Editors often need to meet hard constraints, such as hitting a precise target duration, while also considering semantic objectives, such as preferring engaging content. These two requirements lend themselves to different computational tools, and combining them is non-trivial. Using video editing as a case study, we present a hybrid approach that combines using LLMs to provide semantically relevant labels for video clips with using mixed-integer linear programming to enforce hard constraints and select content. Our approach guarantees millisecond-precise output durations while optimizing for user-specified semantic objectives, such as informativity and topic relevance. Feedback from editors indicates that our tool supports interactive exploration across several video editing goals, including creating interview rough cuts and shortening edited videos for sharing across different platforms.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs.
abstract: Modern task-oriented chatbots present GUI elements alongside natural-language dialogue, yet the agent’s role has largely been limited to interpreting natural-language input as GUI actions and following a linear workflow. In preference-driven, multi-step tasks such as booking a flight or reserving a restaurant, earlier choices constrain later options and may force users to restart from scratch. User preferences serve as the key criteria for these decisions, yet existing agents do not systematically leverage them. We present MAESTRO, which extends the agent’s role from execution to decision support. MAESTRO maintains a shared preference memory that extracts hard and soft preferences from natural-language utterances and provides two mechanisms. Preference-Grounded GUI Adaptation applies in-place operators (augment, sort, filter, and highlight) to the existing GUI according to preference strength, supporting comparison among options. Preference-Guided Workflow Navigation detects conflicts between preferences and available options, proposes backtracking, and records failed paths to avoid revisiting dead ends. Through a controlled experiment (N = 33), we demonstrated that MAESTRO improved decision quality in movie ticketing: final bookings left fewer hard preferences unmet, and users made fewer selections that violated their stated preferences during the process than in the baseline condition, although task success rate and completion time did not differ significantly. In addition, we showed that using MAESTRO in voice mode can increase users’ active engagement as well as their mental burden, revealing the nuanced tension in agentic interaction design for conversational agents with a GUI.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SpatialBlend: Relational Reconstruction for Cross-Space Presence in Heterogeneous Spaces.
abstract: Cross-space presence enables communication between people in different physical spaces as if they were in the same space. The central challenge is spatial heterogeneity: rooms differ in layout, geometry, and affordances, so directly replaying motion or relying on rigid shared layouts can make behavior invalid, unreachable, or hard to interpret. We present SpatialBlend, a runtime system for cross-space presence based on relational reconstruction: the system continuously describes how the user is interacting with nearby people and objects, then reconstructs avatar behavior in the viewer’s room while respecting that room’s geometry and affordances. We implement SpatialBlend in Unity on Meta Quest 3 and evaluate it in the Freeform Collaboration prototype across an office and a living room with different layouts. In a deployment study with 26 participants (13 dyads), continuous shared presence throughout the room improved social presence, continuity, trackability, and spatial coherence over a zone-based baseline. We release SpatialBlend as open source at https://github.com/snuhcs/spatialblend.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ProtoCall: Preemptive Physical Feedback for Sequential Skill Augmentation.
abstract: Mastering sequential skills is essential for everyday and professional tasks such as cooking and assembly. However, executing actions in the correct order and with appropriate timing remains challenging, particularly during transitions between consecutive steps. Existing approaches, including haptic guidance, error-based feedback, or post-error correction, either increase cognitive load, reduce users’ agency, or intervene too late to prevent errors. We developed ProtoCall, a custom wearable physical feedback system, combined with a Vision–Language Model (VLM) for interaction inference, and designed three feedback strategies targeting different stages of the error process: 1) preemptive attentional nudging (attention-level guidance by head actuation), 2) preemptive reaching nudging (action-level prevention of reaching), and 3) post-error nudging. We conducted a user study with 16 participants on a sequential step-transition task, revealing trade-offs between physical feedback strategies across augmentation, retention, and user experience.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Fold2Unfold: Screen Privacy Protection against Shoulder Surfing using Inter-Screen Reflection on Foldable Smartphones.
abstract: Smartphone use in crowded public spaces exposes users to shoulder surfing, allowing nearby bystanders to easily access privacy-sensitive information on the screen. We present Fold2Unfold, a screen privacy protection system for foldable smartphones that ensures screen content readable only from the user’s viewpoint without additional hardware. Fold2Unfold decomposes the original content into two complementary, individually illegible shares displayed across screens, and leverages inter-screen reflection to reconstruct the content. By tracking the user’s eye position and dynamically warping the content accordingly, the system ensures that the reconstructed content is readable only to the user. We implement Fold2Unfold on a commercial foldable device and evaluate its usability and security through controlled user studies involving a PIN entry task. Our results show that Fold2Unfold substantially reduces information leakage under shoulder surfing, with attackers inferring only 6.5% shown on a 10-digit keypad, while incurring a modest input time increase compared to our baseline keypad.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: InvisIto: Weaving Unobtrusive Infrared Markers for Ubiquitous Textile Interaction.
abstract: Textiles are increasingly explored as media for interacting with digital information. However, many of the existing approaches rely on visible tags, printed overlays, or electronic modules that compromise the fabric’s aesthetic and tactile qualities. To address this, we present InvisIto, a method for weaving visually unobtrusive yet machine-readable infrared markers directly into fabrics using near-infrared (NIR)-absorbing yarns. Although these yarns look similar to standard fibers in ambient light, they produce strong contrast in NIR imaging. Our method includes: (1) a design tool that helps users easily embed infrared markers into weaving drafts, (2) five disguising strategies that further reduce marker visibility under ambient light, and (3) a camera-based detection pipeline for decoding and tracking the woven markers. InvisIto supports both woven QR codes for data encoding and woven ArUco markers for binary input and deformation tracking. We demonstrate applications across hand weaving, Jacquard weaving, and industrial fabrication, showing that InvisIto supports interaction and fabrication across scales, from bespoke artifacts to mass production.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: HapTap: Ultrashort, Low Power Pulses for Localized Fingertip Haptics.
abstract: Linear-resonant actuators (LRAs) are typically designed for longer (100 ms) vibrations that feel spatially diffuse when coupled to the skin. In this work, we investigate ultra-short (1 ms) actuation signals using miniature (6 mm diameter) LRAs to create more focused fingertip sensations. To study the transition from diffuse vibrations to localized pulses, we first characterized actuator motion, then conducted a broad perceptual study followed by a targeted psychophysical evaluation. Physically, higher voltage (12 V vs 5 V) but shorter, quarter-cycle pulses produced slightly higher peak displacement (1.7X) and substantially higher estimated indentation force (4.9X) when compared to a baseline driving signal, though only for one polarity. Perceptually, shorter real and perceived durations increased the sense of pulse concentration and slightly improved valence. Finally, with 8 actuators arranged in a 2X4 array, our 1 ms pulses achieved higher localization accuracy than a 119 ms sinusoidal stimulus (71.6% vs. 61.9%) while using 9.6X less energy.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PressMic: Multi-Level Press Input on Commodity Devices Using Built-in Microphones.
abstract: We present PressMic, a passive acoustic method that enables multi-level press input on commodity devices using built-in microphones. PressMic introduces a notched annulus around the microphone vent, forming a compact press-sensitive acoustic interface. Upon finger contact, the device enclosure and the annular boundary create a local acoustic configuration near the vent. A light press produces a detectable resonance from the front cavity, whereas a hard press blocks the vent and suppresses acoustic coupling. PressMic uses a two-stage, event-driven signal pipeline that first detects press events and then classifies them as light or hard. We validate the mechanism with controlled cavity-variation experiments and evaluate the system on a commodity smartphone under ambient sound levels ranging from 25 to 85 dB. Under these conditions, the first-stage detector achieves 96.1% accuracy, the second-stage classifier 95.9%, and the complete pipeline 94.2% accuracy with a Macro-F1 score of 0.932 for three-state recognition. These results demonstrate that passive acoustic modulation using built-in microphones—especially noise-canceling or array types—enables multi-level press input with only a low-profile, cleanable structure around the vent, without active sensing or extra sensors.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: EvoMaestro: Toward Interpretable and Steerable LLM-Driven Program Evolution.
abstract: Recent program evolution systems use large language models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively improve populations of programs, producing striking advances in mathematics, algorithm design, and scientific computing. Yet these systems largely operate as fully automated black boxes. As populations grow, domain experts must make sense of the scores, code changes, reasoning, and algorithmic ideas across many programs, while current interfaces provide limited support for understanding or redirecting the evolution. We characterize this need to understand and steer populations of evolving algorithmic ideas as semantic oversight. A formative study with 8 domain experts yields six design requirements for this emerging human-computer interaction problem. We then propose a steerable program evolution framework that lets expert judgments shape subsequent evolution. Built on this framework, EvoMaestro is an interactive visual analytics system that organizes evolution information from population overview to source code. It helps experts locate and compare noteworthy programs, guide evolution with natural language, combine promising ideas, and prune unproductive directions. A seven-day system demonstration illustrates how an expert applied these capabilities throughout a long-running evolution process. A within-subjects study with 12 participants shows that EvoMaestro improves users’ understanding of evolution processes, reduces cognitive workload, and supports expert steering. These findings suggest that preserving expert agency in open-ended LLM-driven search requires support for both informed judgment and the ability to shape subsequent automation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Supporting The Many Lives of Personal Data with Rebite: LLM-Powered Goal-Directed Framing in Food Journaling.
abstract: People’s health and tracking goals frequently change, but most personal informatics systems struggle to adapt, leading people to abandon their data and start over. We propose goal-directed framing, an approach that repositions goals within personal informatics systems. Instead of fixing the meaning of data at capture time, the approach frames the collected data through the current goal and reframes it whenever the goal changes. We realize this in Rebite, a photo-based food journaling system that uses LLMs to read unstructured meal photos and produce goal-directed feedback. In a one-week deployment with 21 participants managing multiple dietary goals, we find that goal-directed framing shaped how participants engaged with their goals. Translating a goal into metrics helped them see what it meant in practice, confirming existing priorities, surfacing what they overlooked, and revealing where the metrics fell short. When goals changed, seeing past meals reframed under the new goal exposed overlaps and conflicts, prompting participants to negotiate trade-offs and refine priorities. We discuss how goal-directed framing both supports and complicates reflection as goals change, and offer design implications for personal informatics systems to support evolving goals.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Simulating Word Suggestion Usage in Mobile Typing to Guide Intelligent Text Entry Design.
abstract: Intelligent text entry (ITE) methods, such as word suggestions, are widely used in mobile typing, yet improving these systems remains challenging because the cognitive mechanisms underlying suggestion use are poorly understood and evaluating new systems often requires long-term user studies to account for behavioral adaptation. We present WSTypist, a reinforcement learning-based model that simulates how typists integrate word suggestions into typing. We extend recent hierarchical control models of typing by identifying and implementing important cognitive mechanisms that underlie high-level decision-making when integrating word suggestions into manual typing: considering orthographic processes, assessing efficiency gains, and accounting for personal preferences regarding AI support. Our evaluations show that WSTypist simulates diverse human-like suggestion-use strategies, reproduces behavioral differences, and generalizes across different systems. Through four design cases, we demonstrate how a computational rationality model can inform what-if analyses during the design process by simulating how users might adapt to changes in the UI or algorithmic support, thereby reducing the need for user studies early in the exploratory design phase.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Co-Annotator: Expert-Distilled ViT and VLM for Visual and Documentation Guidance in Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
abstract: Clinical AI often optimizes predictive performance without engaging how clinicians decide where to look and what to write. We present Co-Annotator, which distills expert gaze and dictation into two guidance components: a gaze-aligned Vision Transformer producing fixation-aligned areas of interest (AOIs), and an ontology-bounded vision–language model (VLM) that pre-fills editable biomarker summaries for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT). We first collect expert gaze and dictations (US1) to train the models, significantly improving diagnostic accuracy and biomarker generation. We then deploy the system with ophthalmology residents: a controlled resident study (US2) confirmed each modality is safe and independently beneficial, with AOI guidance producing lasting perceptual efficiency gains through post-guidance carryover and VLM guidance more than doubling biomarker documentation breadth. In a combined deployment across two academic institutions (US3), providing both modalities simultaneously produced efficiency gains that substantially exceeded either modality alone: correct diagnoses per minute increased by 40% and comment editing time fell by 67%, without compromising diagnostic accuracy. Notably, neither modality improved efficiency during guidance in US2, which makes the in-guidance efficiency gain under combined guidance in US3 the more striking result. Expert-distilled multimodal guidance can remove two distinct clinical workflow bottlenecks at once (visual search overhead and documentation burden) without compromising the diagnostic accuracy clinicians already achieve.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Augmenting Human Performance with an XR Agent Learning from Online Behavior and BCI Evidence.
abstract: We present OLIVE, a framework for adapting a foundation model to provide real-time assistance in temporally demanding, high-stakes, and dynamic tasks. We show that passive EEG, fused online with behavioral evidence, can meaningfully extend the number of targets users detect and engage beyond their unaided action bandwidth. OLIVE learns from both explicit behavioral signals (the targets the user shoots down in an XR first-person shooter game) and implicit physiological signals (fixation-locked EEG) to provide timely guidance, continuously adapting a frozen vision–language model’s inference on which items are task-relevant by jointly estimating per-source reliability without manual labels or offline training. Through three user studies, including two live deployments of an assistive agent driven by OLIVE in XR, we show that OLIVE Pareto-dominates prior test-time adaptation frameworks, achieving the highest convergence rate at comparable convergence speed. Combining implicit physiological and explicit behavioral signals, the OLIVE agent produces the largest and most reliable within-session improvement to a user’s ability to detect and engage targets, largely independent of the individual’s skill. When the target switches silently, the agent that uses both behavioral and physiological signals reconverges significantly faster than the behavior-only agent (1.27 times faster on average, p =.008), restoring trustworthy guidance at the moment the task changes, precisely when reliable assistance matters most.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: StitchSwitch: Programmable Surface Deformation and Bistability in Embroidered Textiles.
abstract: Programming 3D surface deformation has been widely explored in rigid and semi-rigid materials, but achieving predictable shape change in wearable textiles remains challenging. We present StitchSwitch, a computational design and fabrication system for programming surface deformation and bistability into embroidered textiles through a continuous parametric tessellation design space. Embroidering triangle-tessellated patches onto pre-stretched elastic fabric encodes out-of-plane deformation and passive bistability directly into the textile. We characterize how patch diameter and embroidery fill percentage govern deformation, revealing varied deformation outcomes and a saturation regime where increasing density shifts deformation from vertical height to lateral distribution. We develop a reduced-space simulation model predicting this relationship in real time, integrated into a garment-scale design tool supporting live 3D preview, inverse design, and fabrication-aware export. We demonstrate StitchSwitch through two garment-integrated applications, a tactile garment interface and a deformation-based storage pocket, showing how programmable bistable deformation enables functional structures directly within textiles.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ElectroPad: Extending Gamepad Haptics for Hand Movements in Video Games with Electrotactile Feedback.
abstract: Gamepads are among the most widely used haptic devices, yet their haptic feedback remains limited in supporting hand-movement scenarios in video games that require precise tactile sensations at specific hand locations. Electrotactile feedback offers a promising alternative, providing high-resolution, precisely mapped stimulation that can be seamlessly integrated onto controller surfaces.
