We present ElectroPad, an electrotactile gamepad cover embedding 190 electrodes per handle, delivering rich texture and shape feedback to hand regions in contact with virtual objects. Two user studies demonstrate that our system reliably conveys tactile cues, achieving mid-to-high levels of realism, while significantly enhancing enjoyment and immersion compared to visual-only conditions. Participants also expressed strong willingness to adopt the system and offered concrete suggestions for refinement. These findings highlight electrotactile stimulation as a powerful complement to gamepad haptics, expanding the design space for game interactions and enabling more expressive user experiences.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: BlimpMate: A Quiet, Long-Endurance Flying Display for Hands-Free Intelligent Interaction.
abstract: Digital information in everyday environments is still primarily accessed through fixed or handheld screens, which often divert attention away from ongoing physical activity. Flying displays offer an alternative by positioning information directly in three-dimensional space, near the user and near the task. However, most existing aerial interfaces rely on multirotor drones, whose noise, limited endurance, and exposed propellers make them less suitable for calm, sustained indoor interaction. We present BlimpMate, a long-endurance flying display robot for hands-free intelligent interaction in everyday indoor environments. Built on a helium blimp platform that provides passive buoyant lift, BlimpMate supports quiet and energy-efficient operation while integrating a lightweight projection-based display, multimodal sensing, custom low-level flight control, and a networked interaction stack with AI-supported services. Its display architecture enables a large-area, visually expressive onboard display while remaining compatible with the severe payload constraints of a small indoor blimp. Rather than using the blimp as a passive carrier, we frame it as a mobile visual interface that supports controlled repositioning near users and task locations. Through technical characterization and proof-of-concept scenarios, we position blimp-based flying displays as a promising platform for calm, persistent, and spatially situated indoor interaction beyond conventional screens and drone-based platforms.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MaterialVellum: Steering Generative AI by Leveraging Expressive Material Affordances to Form Design Constraints.
abstract: We present MaterialVellum, an interaction approach for steering generative AI through material-inspired manipulation of design constraints. In urban design, for instance, zoning bounds can be defined by the stretch of elastic bands, building density redistributed by molding clay, and functional relationships organized by the pull of magnets. MaterialVellum departs from current interfaces that rely on natural language prompts, and instead leverages users’ existing knowledge of physical materials to represent and manipulate design constraints. We introduce a framework that maps material affordances—such as elasticity, malleability, or attraction—to spatial, relational, and proportional constraints that underpin design. These mappings are operationalized in user interfaces through familiar direct manipulation multi-touch gestures, including stretching, sculpting, and clustering, whose effects feed as control parameters into generative AI pipelines. We demonstrate this approach through technology probes, including an urban design, a flower arrangement design, and a graphical design scenario. A qualitative study (N=10) shows that material-based interactions improve accessibility of constraint expression, support exploratory workflows, and lower barriers for non-experts, while effectiveness depends on alignment with users’ mental models.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: WhatIf: Interactive Exploration of Large-Scale LLM Agent Simulations for Policy Reasoning.
abstract: Policymakers in domains such as emergency management, public health, and urban planning must make decisions under deep uncertainty, where outcomes depend on how large populations interpret information, coordinate, and adopt over time. Existing tools only partially support this process: tabletop exercises enable collaborative discussion but lack dynamic feedback, while computational simulations capture population dynamics but are designed for offline analysis. We present WhatIf, an interactive system that enables policymakers to steer, inspect, and compare LLM-powered social simulations in real time. Informed by a formative study in emergency preparedness planning, we derive four design requirements for interactive policy simulations: fluid steering, real-time scale, collaborative exploration, and multi-level interpretability. We developed WhatIf guided by these requirements and evaluated it with five preparedness professionals across three disaster evacuation scenarios. Our findings show that participants used the system as a space for iterative branching and comparison rather than evaluating fixed plans; reflected on tacit planning assumptions when agent behavior violated expectations; surfaced previously unrecognized planning vulnerabilities; and grounded their reasoning in inspectable agent-level cases rather than aggregate outputs alone. These findings suggest broader design implications for LLM-powered social simulation systems: designing such systems as interactive, shared reasoning environments—rather than offline predictive tools—can better support expert decision-making under deep uncertainty.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Electrotactile Improves Thermal Referral.
abstract: Thermal referral enables thermal sensations in locations lacking thermal actuators—this is achieved using vibrotactile actuators to redirect a nearby thermal sensation to where a tactile sensation is applied. However, we found that its reliance on vibration introduces critical limitations: it struggles to produce cold referral, and the inherent strong tactile “buzz” makes it unsuitable for simulating non-contact thermal events, such as the chill of an open freezer in VR (in contrast to contact-based thermal events like touching the freezer’s cold handle). To improve this, we propose a shift from vibrotactile to electrotactile-based thermal referral. We evaluated in two user studies—a psychophysics experiment (N=22) and a VR deployment (N=20)—where we contrasted electrotactile with vibrotactile-based thermal referral. Our results reveal key advantages of the electrotactile-based thermal referral: (1) increases the referral rate for cold sensations; (2) increases thermal perception while minimizing tactile; and (3) improves realism across a range of VR thermal scenarios, specifically distinguishing between contact-based and non-contact thermal events. Finally, we provide design guidelines for choosing tactile cues to create immersive multi-modal thermal experiences in VR.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Spatula: Exploring On-Demand In-Situ Interfaces and Interaction for Attribute Control.
abstract: Controlling attributes is a critical step toward achieving the final creative outcome, yet current approaches fall short in supporting users in the iterative refinement of generative content. We propose Spatula, a proof-of-concept system that generates on-demand, in-situ attribute control interfaces and interactions for creating motion graphics. Building on a technical probe that automatically analyzes animation context and generates corresponding attributes and UI, we frame attribute control as an explorable landscape and explore the attribute control space along four key dimensions: Discoverability, Resolution, Scope, and Expandability. Findings from a user study (N=12) show that our system provides intuitive and convenient interactions while supporting diverse needs for fine-grained parameter control. Furthermore, our applications demonstrate that the plug-and-play design generalizes to other domains, such as web design and 3D modeling.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: LandmarkLens: Predicting and Presenting Effective Landmarks for Mixed-Reality Urban Exploration.
abstract: People with a poor sense of direction (SOD) struggle to build cognitive maps for effective spatial navigation, and existing navigation tools prioritize efficiency over spatial learning. To understand how navigation strategies differ by ability, we conducted a landmark attention study with 20 participants (ten good SOD, ten poor SOD) who navigated across four Tokyo neighborhoods in virtual reality (VR). We found systematic group differences in both gaze behavior and the types of landmarks they verbally identify as effective. Based on these findings, we built LandmarkLens, a mixed-reality (MR) navigation system that uses a vision-language model (VLM) to identify and highlight navigation-relevant landmarks. A follow-up study with eight poor-SOD participants showed improved performance in scene recognition, suggesting that guided landmark attention can support landmark-level spatial knowledge acquisition for people with poor SOD, a first step toward broader spatial learning.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: EITWatch: Smartwatch-Integrated Planar Electrical Impedance Tomography for Hand Gesture Recognition.
abstract: Wrist Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) senses hand gestures from muscle- and tendon-driven impedance changes, but prior wrist-EIT systems require electrode coverage beyond the watch-back contact patch and separate analog front ends. We present EITWatch, the first wrist-EIT system built around smartwatch case-back geometry, asking whether this contact patch alone can support gesture recognition: eight planar electrodes in a 31 mm ring acquire 35 impedance measurements at 48 Hz. Because a planar array cannot encircle the wrist, EITWatch uses multi-depth scanning to sample multiple source-sink distances and current paths; it beat matched adjacent injection by 15.1/10.4 percentage points (macro/micro) across all 12 participants. In a prompted study, within-session leave-one-round-out accuracy reached 91.4%/92.5% (window/trial) for six macro-gestures, and 90.1%/91.5% (window/segment) for five micro-gestures plus relax; window-level cross-session and leave-one-user-out transfer reached 73.2%/70.4% and 63.1%/55.3% (macro/micro).
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Generative Proxy: Synthesizing Proxy-Based Interfaces for Real-World Interaction Across AR Glasses.
abstract: Interacting with real-world objects in AR is difficult, especially when targets are distant, cluttered, or occluded. These challenges are amplified on emerging lightweight AR glasses, which often lack binocular or large field of view on display, but also continuous inputs, such as hand or eye tracking. Proxy-based interfaces offer an alternative by allowing users to interact with virtual abstractions of physical objects that can be repositioned, reorganized, and adapted to the task and device. However, designing such interfaces is currently manual and highly device-specific. We present Generative Proxy, a method for automatically generating proxy-based interfaces from three specifications: scene, intent, and device capabilities. We formulate generation as a constrained synthesis problem that first produces valid interfaces for the target device and task, then ranks candidates using semantic and articulatory distance inspired by direct manipulation theory. We demonstrate Generative Proxy across diverse scenes, device profiles, and user intents. Expert evaluation shows initial evidence that generated proxy UIs are useful and usable, highlighting proxy-based abstraction as a promising interaction paradigm for future AR glasses.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Boosting WiFi-based Gesture Recognition via High-affinity and Behaviorally Diverse Data Synthesis.
abstract: Artificial-intelligence–driven WiFi-based human gesture recognition (HGR) critically depends on high-quality, well-labeled real-world datasets. However, collecting real WiFi data is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Data augmentation (DA) has emerged as an effective strategy to enhance the value of limited real data and improve system generalization. Existing wireless DA methods, however, either cannot generate samples for new gesture classes or fail to capture behavioral diversity sufficiently, fundamentally limiting their scalability to new sensing tasks and augmentation effectiveness. In this work, we propose SynthFi, a novel DA framework capable of synthesizing high-fidelity and diverse WiFi data, even for unseen classes with very few real samples. SynthFi incorporates two key components: a diversity-inducing factor quantification method that extracts rich behavioral variation cues from limited data, and a diffusion-based generative model that produces realistic samples conditioned on diverse behavioral features. Extensive real-world experiments show that SynthFi can improve recognition accuracy by \(40\%\) through DA, even when only two real samples of unseen classes are available, outperforming existing solutions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: A Text-Native Interface for Generative Video Authoring.
abstract: Everyone can write their stories in freeform text format – it’s something we all learn in school, yet authoring video requires one to learn specialized and complicated tools. In this paper, we introduce Doki, a text-native interface for generative video authoring. In Doki, writing text is the primary interaction: within a single document, users define assets, structure scenes, generate shots, refine edits, and add audio. We articulate the design principles of this text-native approach and demonstrate Doki’s capabilities through examples. We ran a week-long diary study with 10 participants of varied expertise. Participants produced 46 videos, reporting faster idea‑to‑draft flow, improved coherence through parameterization, and clearer comprehension of narrative structure in the document view; they also surfaced limitations around model predictability, precise control, and temporal expressivity. With Doki, we explore a fundamental shift in generative video interfaces, and demonstrate a powerful and accessible new way to craft visual stories.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MetaBeads: Enabling Shape- and Stiffness-Changing Interfaces through Beaded Metamaterials.
abstract: As interactive systems increasingly extend into the physical world, designers need accessible ways to prototype interfaces that can change both shape and stiffness. In this paper, we investigate how simple, widely available materials—beads and string—can be used to construct shape- and stiffness-changing interfaces without specialized machinery. We introduce a set of reusable structural mechanisms that enable sturdy, wearable, and load-bearing structures from bead-based assemblies, each supporting a distinct mode of deformation and stiffness change, such as transforming from a flexible sheet into a jammed cuboid, a stiff tube, or a bistable curvature cell. To facilitate the creation of these structures, we provide an interactive design tool that guides craftspeople designing and fabricating their own MetaBead interfaces. We demonstrate the possibilities of MetaBeads through four application prototypes across wearable devices, educational tools, and adaptive furniture. Together, this work offers an accessible approach to prototyping shape- and stiffness-changing interfaces with everyday materials.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: iRing: Rich Interaction on Smart Ring with Multi-point Capacitive Touch Screen.
abstract: Rising interest in smart rings reflects a growing demand for immediate, lightweight interaction. However, prior designs have largely treated rings as input-only interfaces, or devices with limited on-device visualization, fall short in supporting for tightly coupled, direct, and expressive co-located interaction. To bridge this gap, we present iRing, a lightweight (6.4 g), low-cost ($46.43), open-source, and reproducible smart ring platform centered on a capacitive multi-touch display. We design a compact, multi-touch interface using accessible components that fit the ring’s tight form factor. It further integrates a flexible OLED display, BLE micro-controller, IMU, and PPG sensor, supporting both local and remote interaction. To bridge hardware touch sensing and interaction events, we introduce nano interactions—a compact vocabulary that adapts familiar touch primitives for direct, co-located input and visual output on ultra-small, curved surfaces. Nano interactions allow interaction within a single glance–touch cycle, supporting one-handed, low-attention use under motion. We implement a set of applications to explore the design space enabled by multi-touch on a ring. A user study with 12 participants demonstrates reliable touch interaction and provides positive short-term assessments of usability, comfort, and social acceptability, highlighting opportunities for compact interaction surfaces supporting glanceable and on-the-go interaction.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: KeepOut: An Embodied Intervention Using The Posture to Reduce Habitual Smartphone Overuse.
abstract: Existing interventions for smartphone overuse mainly focus on mitigating the behavior, with limited attention to the conditions that sustain it, which may lead to the recurrence of overuse. Habit theory frames these conditions as contextual cues, and we hypothesize that slumped posture may function as one such cue, which we explore as a design opportunity for intervention. We present KeepOut, a continuous embodied intervention that nudges the users towards upright postures. The system links screen luminance to posture, dimming it during slumped posture and restoring it upon upright posture. We evaluated KeepOut in a 4-week field study (N=38), comparing it with a common periodic notification-based method. Results showed that KeepOut significantly reduced both the usage time (-16.5%) and launch frequency (-25.9%) compared with the pre-intervention condition. Drawing on interviews and daily reports, we inspect the reason for KeepOut’s effectiveness, as well as its influence on phone-use behaviors, posture, and broader daily well-being. Our work demonstrates how behavioral states can be incorporated into intervention design, and suggests posture as a potential direction for understanding smartphone overuse.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ChronoMantic: A Natural Language Interface for Interactive Time Series Pattern Query.
abstract: Finding time series patterns is an important problem in finance, healthcare, climatology, and manufacturing, where temporal data analysis informs critical decision-making processes. Existing approaches use examples, sketches, and natural language (NL) for time series pattern querying, but precisely formulating complex queries, inspecting query interpretations, and refining queries iteratively remain challenging. Nevertheless, NL is a promising modality for pattern specification, balancing expressiveness and preciseness while providing an intuitive means of articulating query intent. This paper introduces ChronoMantic, an NL-driven interactive interface for time series pattern querying. The tool provides glyph-based feedback on query interpretation and supports iterative querying through by-example refinement. We illustrate ChronoMantic’s workflow through two usage scenarios, assess its retrieval performance on a manually annotated benchmark, and evaluate its query effectiveness and usability via a two-stage user study.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: KnowTap: A Knowledge-Driven Tool for Fine-Grained Tappability Assessment and Design Iteration of Mobile UIs.
abstract: Visually perceived tappability, defined as the degree to which a static UI component looks interactive, is critical to interface usability and distinct from physical target acquisition, yet existing task-specific models generally provide binary labels. However, designers need finer-grained tappability assessments to make informed modifications during iterative design. To address this, we propose KnowTap, a Figma-compatible interactive tool that predicts continuous perceived-tappability scores from mean human ratings collected on a 0–5 annotation scale, visualizes them in six display bands, and provides optional LLM-generated feedback to suggest context-aware improvements. Using a new dataset of 800 mobile UIs and 9,751 components whose GPT-4o pre-labels were corrected by three independent crowdworker groups, KnowTap combines structured design knowledge, text-derived features, and deep embeddings in a random forest regressor that achieves SRCC.745 and R2.564 under UI-grouped five-fold cross-validation, compared with.646 and.387 for an adapted, randomly initialized Taperception-style ResNet-18 baseline, while offering attribute-level explanations complementary to prior pixel-level saliency. In a within-subjects study with 12 designers, paired comparisons showed higher reported satisfaction and perceived task success and lower mental demand, temporal demand, and frustration in the six-band condition, and independent raters preferred its resulting designs in three of four test UIs. Our research contributes a knowledge-driven tool for continuous perceived-tappability prediction, along with a new dataset, to support Figma-compatible mobile-UI design iteration.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CoNarrate: Computationally Modeling Information Prematureness and Scaffolding the Co-Construction of Patient Narratives in Asynchronous Telehealth.
abstract: Asynchronous telehealth requires patients to self-report their conditions, which serve as the critical basis for subsequent diagnosis and care. However, patients often struggle to articulate all necessary details upfront. This premature information delivery causes prolonged back-and-forth messaging, delayed clinical decisions, and increased physician burden. Comparing 5,000+ initial self-reports with post-consultation logs, we identified five recurring patterns of information prematureness. We model these patterns using the DIBH framework, mapping patient statements into a computable heterogeneous information space (Data, Information, Beliefs, Heuristics). Leveraging this underlying architecture, we developed CoNarrate, an LLM-driven intake system that proactively detects prematureness and generates targeted scaffolding questions before doctor review. A between-subjects study (N=46) demonstrated that CoNarrate significantly improved the clinical information richness of self-reports, reducing follow-up needs while maintaining high user satisfaction. This work contributes a new lens for modeling information prematureness, and a novel algorithmic approach to scaffolding the co-construction of comprehensive medical narratives.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TypeRing: Ten-Finger Surface Typing with Dual IMU Rings.
abstract: Ten-finger surface typing promises a portable alternative to physical keyboards and touchscreens, making it well-suited for mobile scenarios, but remains challenging to balance sensing cost with input performance. We ask whether it can be enabled with two IMU rings, without relying on bulky wearables or continuous vision processing. We first present TypeRingIMU, which detects rapid ten-finger touches and identities with an F1-score of 98.4%, enabling efficient ten-finger typing on any flat surface using only two IMU rings. We further enhance it via optical-inertial fusion that opportunistically detects touch positions from IMU-triggered touch events, leveraging the front-facing camera already available on mobile devices, namely TypeRing. It removes fingering constraints, thus improving input naturalness and accuracy. Our method achieves 28.6 WPM input speed (63.5% of physical keyboards), with top-1 and top-12 accuracies of 88.5% and 98.1%, significantly outperforming current methods and demonstrating strong potential for efficient, convenient, and user-friendly mobile text input.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TapTwice: Rich Offline Interfaces Between NFC-Enabled Devices.
abstract: Applications that rely on the Internet are subject to latency and unstable connectivity. To ensure reliability, applications such as contactless payment are designed to accept offline devices: interfaces are rendered on public terminals, and authorization is completed through simple NFC taps. However, interacting with public devices raises security concerns (i.e. shoulder surfing) and constrains user input. To address these limitations, we present TapTwice, a new interaction technique that relocates the entire process to the user’s smartphone and relies solely on NFC, hence preserving the reliability of offline interaction and providing the ability to render complex interfaces. Users first tap to download an interactive interface via NFC, complete the interaction on their personal device, and then tap again to transmit the results back for finalization. To achieve this design, we modified the NFC software stack on two Google Pixel 6 Pro phones to unlock higher transmission throughput, achieving a link nine times faster than the default. This improvement allows self-contained interfaces to be transferred within seconds. We further demonstrate how leveraging personal smartphones enhances privacy and convenience — for example, by enabling biometric authentication in place of PIN entry and supporting autofill in place of repetitive input across different terminals.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Integrating Visual and Acoustic Modalities for Near-Eye Gaze Tracking.
abstract: Near-eye gaze tracking underpins gaze-based interaction on head-mounted displays, yet the dominant vision-based approach incurs substantial power consumption and computational overhead. Acoustic sensing has recently emerged as a low-power, high-rate alternative, but lacks user-friendly calibration and loses accuracy after device slippage and re-wearing. To address these complementary limitations, we present a dual-modal gaze tracking system that integrates an acoustic module and a visual module on a single eyewear platform. Visual predictions implicitly calibrate and continuously correct the acoustic modality through a state-machine-based coordination strategy, eliminating dedicated acoustic calibration and providing system-level robustness to device slippage and re-wearing. An error-state Kalman filter fuses the two asynchronous modalities to produce the final gaze estimate. When the visual modality operates at 1 Hz, the fused system achieves 1.40° within-session and 2.13° across re-wearing sessions at 83 Hz output rate, close to the sparse visual baseline. When needed, the system allows the visual modality to operate at up to 30 Hz and the acoustic modality at up to 750 Hz, contributing to improvements in overall accuracy and output frame rate.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: DocuDebug: A Graph-Supported Interactive Editor for Verifying and Maintaining Internal Logical Consistency.
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) accelerate report generation, maintaining logical consistency during revisions increases the cognitive load, and delegating this task to LLMs often results in unpredictable global overwrites. To address this, we present DocuDebug, an interactive editor that reframes document verification as a software engineering task. The system models a document’s logical structure and citations as an explicit dependency graph. Through a linter-like interface, users receive real-time warnings for logical conflicts and propagate localized edits with guided precision. In a within-subjects study with 12 professional writers, DocuDebug guided precise, necessary corrections, improving precision over threefold and reducing over-editing from over 40% to under 5%. Furthermore, objective logs revealed that users avoided blind acceptance, actively deliberating over each warning for nearly three minutes. This work demonstrates how structured visual diagnostics can shift AI-assisted writing from opaque global generation to systematic, user-controlled co-creation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Zoro: Active Controls to Support Rule Following in Vibe Coding.
abstract: Rules files (e.g., AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) are the primary mechanism for human-agent alignment when developers vibe code. However, they remain passive: it is not immediately apparent when rules are being used or followed, or how to improve them. To transform rules from passive text into active controls, we introduce Zoro, an interactive interface that integrates directly with a coding agent and anchors rules to every step of the coding process. After an agent generates an initial plan, Zoro enriches the plan with rules, enforces the rules during implementation by requiring the agent to prove that each rule was followed, and allows users to provide in-situ feedback when they are unsatisfied with a rule application to evolve the scope of the rules. A technical evaluation shows that coding agents follow rules more with Zoro than without. A user study demonstrates a change in people’s behavior and cognitive strategies when rules are at the forefront of vibe coding. We discuss how making rules active in agentic systems unlocks broader opportunities for human-agent alignment in coding settings and beyond.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ShadAR: Real-time Prompting On-demand Visual Augmentation in Augmented Reality.
abstract: Augmented Reality can reshape our visual perception (e.g., simulating color blindness) yet such effects are typically pre-programmed by experts, making visual augmentation static and inflexible. We introduce ShadAR, an AR system that allows users to describe expected visual augmentations (e.g., "Blur all people") for changing their vision in real time. ShadAR can graphically manipulate AR passthrough real-time via shader injection. When receiving a user’s prompt, ShadAR uses LLMs (GPT5.2) to interpret the user’s intent, analyzes the user’s view with object detection (YOLOv26), generates a pixel shader, and applies it to the targeted region on AR passthrough. To understand usage pattern, we invited 21 HCI researchers to use ShadAR, identifying four application domains (design, health, productivity, and social interaction) and two prompt-framing patterns: procedural prompts specifying what to modify and how (“Highlight the book.”), and end-goal prompts conveying desired mental/behavioral states (“Make me laugh.”). Such end-goal prompts suggest a future in which users specify outcomes (e.g., “Make me not miss my flight”) while the system determines how to realize them, though often with inherently indeterminate results. We discuss design opportunities for ShadAR and ethical concerns.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PACEE: Parent-Centered AI Scaffolding for Emotion Education in Early Childhood Conversations.
abstract: Emotion education is critical for children aged 3 to 6. However, existing technologies depend substantially on direct child-AI interaction, overlooking the central role of parents in guiding early emotional development at home. To address this gap, we conducted co-design sessions with five kindergarten teachers and five parents to identify key parental challenges and opportunities for AI support in family emotion education. Based on these insights, we developed PACEE, an LLM-based assistant designed around an asymmetric triadic interaction framework: AI primarily supports parents while preserving parent-child interaction. PACEE provides parent-centered AI scaffolding that supports parents in real-time conversation through personalized guidance, post-hoc reflection through trackable feedback, and understanding children’s emotional states through modeling. We evaluated PACEE with 16 families. Results showed that PACEE increased parent-child conversational engagement and improved parents’ overall experience when guiding emotion-related conversations. Together, we contribute an asymmetric triadic interaction framework for AI-supported family education, offering design insights for AI systems that support parents while preserving parent-led parent–child interaction.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Veriscope: Provenance-Aware Verification of LLM Reasoning Artifacts in Conversational Data Analysis.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted by data analysts to perform various analytical tasks within conversational interfaces, owing to their capabilities in code generation and analytical reasoning. Conversational LLMs generate diverse artifacts through multiple reasoning steps and summarize analytical results into insights. Verifying such analysis remains essential yet challenging, as it requires examining both diverse artifacts and the underlying complex reasoning logic, which is not fully addressed by previous work. To facilitate validating LLM-generated results, we present a claim-centered view of analytic provenance and introduce Veriscope, an interactive system that supports fine-grained verification across interconnected artifacts, on-demand tracing of analytic provenance, and modification of analytical results. We formulated our design considerations based on findings derived from a formative study conducted with data analysts (N=6) who have prior experience in verification. We evaluated the effectiveness and usability of our method through a user study (N=18), which demonstrated that Veriscope substantially improves the efficiency of verifying analytical results produced by LLMs. The reliability of LLM-based features was assessed through a technical evaluation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: LightShop: High-Precision Interactive Computational Light Painting.
abstract: Light painting is a photographic technique that integrates light cast by a handheld light source during the capture of a long-exposure photograph. This creates an image roughly equivalent to that of a static light source with geometry matching the captured motion of the light. Unfortunately, light painting is limited by the precision of hand motion, the inability to visualize progress during the painting process, and occlusions caused by the painter during capture. We introduce LightShop: an interactive system that helps users capture high-precision light paintings with a projector and real-time tracking from a head-mounted display (HMD). LightShop helps users compose, pre-visualize, and capture precise light paintings with guidance from augmented reality (AR) interfaces, using a novel computational exposure strategy to isolate light cast by the intended emitter on the scene. We demonstrate that LightShop lets users easily capture complex reflections and refractions among real objects illuminated by precisely constructed virtual light emitters.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Codetations: Rich, Granular, and Maintainable Annotations for Evolving Code.
abstract: Developers accumulate rich contextual knowledge about their code (e.g., design rationales, edge cases, worked examples) that does not fit in source files and goes stale when kept in separate documents or in human memory. We present Codetations, a VSCode extension enabling persistent, interactive annotations on arbitrary code spans without modifying the underlying file. A novel hybrid annotation anchoring method combines editor tracking for local edits with LLM-based semantic matching for offline changes, keeping annotations stable as code evolves. Annotation tools are modules sharing a minimal API for document access and state management. We demonstrate that this API is expressive enough to support multimedia embedding, automatic documentation maintenance, and external tool integration. In initial user studies with nine experienced developers, we found that attachment behavior matched their expectations. The diverse tools also enabled developers to imagine a variety of domain-specific use cases for annotations, particularly for validating and managing LLM-generated code. We discuss how a lightweight annotation layer can preserve contextual knowledge and open up a novel design space of developer-defined annotations.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Relative-Motion-Aware Color Presentation with High-Speed Projection.
abstract: This paper proposes a color image display method where the perceived image changes according to the viewer’s direction of movement relative to the display surface. Conventional motion-responsive displays require camera-based tracking, which poses challenges for privacy and scalability in public spaces. To address this, we propose a display method that leverages the relative motion between the viewer and the display surface without any sensors. The system can present different images for two arbitrary directions of the viewer’s movement. This is achieved by temporally decomposing target images and reintegrating them through high-speed projection, enabling motion-contingent display without external sensors. We describe the mechanism for inducing specific color perception during movement and evaluate image fidelity through experiments. Furthermore, we implement a digital signage application and conduct user studies to discuss its effectiveness. Our approach enables adaptive signage that responds to movement direction without the need for complex tracking systems.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Camera-Free Object Discovery and Interaction with GazeTags.
abstract: We present GazeTags, a camera- and computer-vision-free approach for worn head-gaze object awareness. Our small electronic tags cost roughly $2 each and can operate for more than a year on a coin cell battery. They work in concert with a user-worn device (smartglasses, hearables, etc.) that periodically emits a focused infrared signal aligned with the user’s head direction. Only GazeTags within that narrow head-oriented beam wake and respond, providing their identity and optional payloads such as object state or live sensor readings. By avoiding cameras and computer vision pipelines, our approach is very energy efficient, able to operate continuously even in battery-constrained wearables, and sidesteps non-trivial privacy issues. We describe our hardware design, characterize our system performance and operating tradeoffs, and demonstrate how GazeTags can enable practical gaze-aware environments.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: LinkHydro: Design and Rapid Fabrication of Soft Self-Pumping Tubes for Prototyping Hydraulic Interface.
abstract: Liquid-based interfaces offer rich expressive capabilities but are often constrained by bulky and noisy hydraulic systems, limiting their use in interactive applications. Recent fiber-based pumps integrate actuation into tubes, enabling silent and compact fluid control, yet they remain difficult to fabricate, design, and deploy in rapid prototyping scenarios. To address these challenges, we present LinkHydro, a method for designing and rapidly fabricating soft self-pumping tubes based on electrohydrodynamics (EHD). By leveraging heat-shrink tubing and a simple fabrication process, LinkHydro enables on-demand production of pumps in approximately 10 minutes. We further introduce a design support tool that allows users to parametrize pump characteristics such as pressure without requiring specialized knowledge. LinkHydro supports modular reconfiguration of tubes, enabling intuitive and tangible control of liquid behavior. We evaluate fabrication time, design support, pumping performance, and silent operation, and demonstrate application scenarios that highlight its potential for prototyping hydraulic interfaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MorphoChrome: Interactive, Handheld Fabrication of Programmable Structural Color.
abstract: Surfaces that change color with viewing angle—from select butterfly wings and hummingbird feathers to passport holograms—communicate, authenticate, and display information without power or pigment. This is possible through structural color: vivid, view-dependent color produced by nanoscale geometry rather than pigment. However, existing methods for producing structural color are highly complex, lab-bound, and offer no direct user control over color output, color mixing, or angular encoding. We present MorphoChrome, a novel handheld optical system and workflow for interactive, programmable structural color fabrication. By exposing a holographic photopolymer film to user-controlled wavelengths and angles of coherent light, MorphoChrome directly inscribes the nanostructures required to produce iridescent color. Within the device, red, green, and blue laser diodes mix via optical beam combining to generate mixed color outputs. The device can be controlled either independently or through a digital twin user interface that provides physics-informed, live iridescent preview, and precise color selection for RGB color mixing. We evaluate MorphoChrome’s color gamut, color quality, resolution, and sub-second fabrication speed. We introduce a new resin-based adhesion process for integrating holographic films with 2D and 3D objects of diverse material composition (from PLA to fabric), and demonstrate a range of designs produced by our system through applications for colorimetric sensing, security, and biomimetic design.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: OpenGut: An Open-Source Platform for Gut-Computer Interaction Research.
abstract: Researchers are increasingly exploring the gut as a human-computer interface due to its gut-brain axis, linking physiological states with emotion and cognition. Despite its potential, the gut research space remains highly fragmented and underexplored. This is largely due to the absence of open and accessible hardware and software tools that could enable systematic investigation across disciplines and communities. To address this gap, we conducted semi-structured interviews with six experts to identify pain points in using existing platforms. Based on the themes identified, we formulated a set of requirements, and developed OpenGut, a rapid prototyping platform for gut research. Our open source platform consists of three main components: a wearable hardware platform for data capture and playback, a graphical user interface for visualization and analysis, as well as accompanying documentation for platform setup and customization. We perform technical evaluation of OpenGut for its signal quality, noise suppression, as well as outline potential usage scenarios for gut research.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Thin-Film Actuator Embedded Haptic Glove Supporting Thumb Kinematics for Displaying Volumetric Shape and Contact Indentation.
abstract: The dexterity of the human hand is fundamentally rooted in the coordination of the thumb’s opposition and adduction. Despite its significance, conventional haptic gloves often neglect these two degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) movements, typically providing only single-channel tactile or force feedback. This limitation severely diminishes realism and control during dexterous manipulation in virtual reality (VR) and teleoperation. In this paper, we present a compact, lightweight haptic glove capable of providing 2-DOF force (kinesthetic) and pressure (tactile) feedback specifically for the thumb. To achieve this, we developed a system that utilizes thin-film electrostatic clutches and a cross-tendon structure to effectively constrain thumb movements. Furthermore, to accommodate varying contact points on the thumb pad during diverse grasping tasks, we integrated two thin-film flexure actuators to deliver localized pressure feedback at two thumb-pad locations. A preliminary user study suggests that constraining 2-DOF thumb movements improves perceived realism and reduces visual–haptic discord during virtual grasping of a cylindrical object with self-selected postures. We further demonstrate the feasibility of the system for stabilizing grasping in the teleoperation of a humanoid hand.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: The Future of 5DOF Laser Cutting Is Personal.
abstract: There has been a recent advent of diode-based laser cutters and a significant uptake among makers. In this paper, we reason that this new technology will also lower the bar for making laser cutters capable of tilting their heads, creating the opportunity to bring 5DOF laser cutting to makers. We anticipate this evolution and present a prototype of a diode-based 5DOF laser cutter built on technology available to makers today. Using this prototype, we explore how to embed 5DOF cutting into makers’ existing software ecosystem to ease adoption. We tackle this by starting from a popular toolchain and then, step-by-step, extending every program, file format, and workflow to 5DOF: We present a 5DOF variant of SVG, we extend Adobe Illustrator with a plugin, and we present a converter for 3D models. We then use our prototype and toolchain to explore what future makers might fabricate using such machines, including hidden joints that provide models with a clean look, load-bearing joints that take 5.8x times higher loads, and cut-in-place mechanisms.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: RampEMS: Onset Shaping for Stroke-Stable Pressure Modulation in Calligraphy.
abstract: Electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) can modulate force during ongoing voluntary action, but abrupt onset can evoke involuntary motion that perturbs fine motor control. We formalize pulse-width onset shaping as an EMS design dimension and implement it as RampEMS, which gradually increases pulse width to a target value instead of applying that value abruptly. Using brush calligraphy as an artifact-producing testbed, a formative study empirically characterized logarithmic onset curvatures and selected a 1-s profile as a task-specific balance between onset smoothing and timely force buildup. We then evaluated this selected profile in a controlled traced-calligraphy study with the characters Ei and San, comparing it with step-type EMS (StepEMS) at the same target pulse width and with noEMS. For Ei, RampEMS significantly increased brush pressure relative to noEMS; for San, RampEMS did not significantly decrease brush pressure relative to noEMS. For both characters, RampEMS produced significantly smaller noEMS-relative stroke error distances than StepEMS, indicating less EMS-associated positional perturbation rather than improvement over unassisted writing. RampEMS also yielded significantly higher SUS scores and lower Raw NASA-TLX scores than StepEMS. Together, these results support pulse-width onset shaping as a task-specific strategy for reducing trajectory disruption during ongoing fine-motor action.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SpeLL: A Generative Framework for Synthesizing 3D Visual Effects from Text Prompts with Large Language Models.
abstract: Creating visual effects (VFX) for 3D content requires specialized design knowledge and technical expertise. Existing methods focus on creating VFX for videos or exploring designs for novices, while professional workflows need frameworks producing complete parameterized 3D assets. This study presents SpeLL, a generative framework that produces editable 3D VFX drafts from text prompts using large language models and retrieval-based asset assembly. A formative study with professional VFX designers identified three design requirements: preference for simplified prompting, need for VFX-specialized assets, and manual spatial-temporal coordination. SpeLL addresses these through prompt enhancement, a spatial design module for component retrieval and layout arrangement, and a temporal design module for activation sequencing. A user study with twenty professional designers evaluated SpeLL against ablated frameworks, 3D generation baselines, and manual workflows. Results showed SpeLL scored higher on intention alignment, spatial-temporal layout quality, and editability, and reduced the effort needed to reach editable VFX structures. Participants valued parameterized outputs over visual complexity, emphasizing workflow integration and manual refinement. These findings indicate that combining LLM reasoning with retrieval-based asset assembly can support early exploration and drafting in professional VFX workflows, while leaving final expressive control to designers.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Body Sublimation: Designing State-Changing Extended Hand for Embodied Out-of-Reach Interaction.
abstract: Recent research in extended reality (XR) and robotics has explored approaches for extending human reach beyond the inert physical body. XR enables embodied interaction with distant targets but lacks physical manipulation. In contrast, robot-mediated systems enable real-world interaction but often disrupt embodiment due to physical constraints such as latency, limited workspace, kinematic mismatch, and collision avoidance. Therefore, reconciling physical manipulation with perceptual embodiment remains an open challenge. In this paper, we present Body Sublimation, an interaction concept that integrates the perceptual flexibility of XR with the physical capabilities of robotic systems. A virtual hand in XR serves as the user’s extended body while both the original hand and robotic manipulator are hidden using diminished reality. A hidden robotic hand then performs physical manipulation, offloading the physical constraints from the user’s perception, thereby maintaining embodiment continuity. We validate the Body Sublimation approach through a user study against a pass-through baseline, where the robot body is always visible, and application scenarios. Compared with a pass-through baseline in which the robot remains visible, our approach maintains task performance while improving trajectory efficiency in obstacle-reaching scenarios, and contributes to a stronger sense of embodiment.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Dishplay: Edible Display Utilizing Magnetic Response of Iron in Cereal.
abstract: This paper presents Dishplay, an edible display system that uses external permanent magnets to generate and animate visual patterns in liquid by actuating iron-fortified cereal. Dishplay supports both static pattern formation through magnet placement and dynamic pattern transitions enabled by a linear actuator–driven magnet array. Through technical evaluations, we examine how cereal quantity, liquid type and volume, and elapsed time affect display fidelity and characterize transition dynamics such as speed and precision. Based on these results, we derive design considerations for visual fidelity and transition behavior and explore application scenarios.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: FlexiFab: Laser-Cutting Volumetric Compliant Structures with Tunable-Stiffness.
abstract: Laser cutting is a powerful fabrication tool for rapidly creating 3D objects from 2D sheet materials. While most research has focused on making these constructions robust and rigid, we expand this area by introducing robust yet compliant laser-cut structures. We present FlexiFab, a method for fabricating load-bearing volumetric objects with tunable stiffness. The core of our approach is to utilize planar lattice structures for programmable compliance, integrated into a robust framework via an orthogonal interlocking assembly. By interlocking these elements, the planar sheets provide mutual lateral support that prevents out-of-plane buckling and structural failure. We also incorporate standard threaded nuts into the assembly, which not only provide structural reinforcement but also allow users to customize local or global stiffness post-fabrication. We demonstrate these benefits through applications such as an adjustable bike seat and provide a parametric design tool to facilitate the end-to-end design process.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MagToTheFuture: Transforming Passive Objects into Circuit-Free Haptic Devices via Magnetic Fields.
abstract: We present MagToTheFuture, a tabletop system that uniquely integrates co-located force, vibration, and thermal feedback to passive objects via magnetic fields, without any onboard electronics. Prior magnetic approaches faced a physical limitation in that coil designs optimized for strong magnetic force inherently conflict with the conditions required for efficient induction heating, thereby restricting the use of multiple co-located modalities. MagToTheFuture accommodates this electromagnetic characteristic by placing a force–vibration coil and a thermal coil together within a single actuator structure while driving the two coils independently. A hall-sensor array estimates patch position and identity, while a linear motion system positions the actuator to deliver force, vibration, and localized heating at a single site. Technical evaluations validate reliable sensing accuracy and haptic outputs across materials, demonstrating the feasibility of augmenting everyday objects into interactive interfaces. User studies showed that multimodal feedback improved four dimensions of the haptic experience in Content Augmentation and Object-Embedded Augmentation, while improving two dimensions in Informational Augmentation. These results highlight the potential of our approach to support more expressive, scalable, and accessible interactive systems.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: The Rock Can Talk: Spatial AI and XR for Rock Climbing Navigation.
abstract: We present RockXR, a mixed reality prototype that examines the potential for approaches like Worlds-in-Miniature (WiM), spatial route annotations, and conversational assistants to provide navigation cues and guidance during rock climbs. These three techniques mirror the combination of overview maps, situated overlays, and conversational turn-by-turn instructions that are increasingly common for pedestrian and car navigation. They also illustrate the growing potential for mixed reality visualization and guidance across technical sports and activities. RockXR uses annotated digital models of climbing routes to render navigation information directly on the wall via a mixed-reality headset, while also providing persistent WiM overviews of the entire route. We also demonstrate how live 3rd person imagery generated from those digital models can support conversational interactions with route descriptions, allowing climbers to “talk to the rock” for guidance and feedback while climbing. To probe the potential of these approaches and gauge climbers’ receptiveness to them, we evaluated RockXR with 16 climbers in a controlled indoor study and complemented this with a field test on an outdoor multi-pitch climb. Our findings highlight the value of flexible guidance interfaces that span multiple reference frames and interaction modalities, and suggest that XR can meaningfully augment how climbers plan, interpret, and move through complex, high-risk terrain.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MoTUI: Personalization of In-Vehicle Tactile Interfaces for People With Vision Impairments and the Blind.
abstract: Configuring in-vehicle interfaces for people with vision impairments (VIPs) requires jointly tuning buttons, feedback modalities, layout, and speech parameters. This defines a design space too large for manual exploration, with inherently conflicting objectives such as maximizing situation awareness while minimizing cognitive load. Prior work recognizes personalization as critical but offers no systematic method to achieve it. We contribute MoTUI, an open-source Modular Tactile User Interface with reconfigurable hardware and software for runtime exploration of this design space and replication of existing designs. MoTUI is configuration-agnostic and supports multiple personalization strategies; we instantiate and evaluate one, pairing it with Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization (HITL-MOBO) to navigate the space efficiently. In a within-subject study (N = 12 VIPs), HITL-optimized configurations outperformed a static baseline and an LLM-generated design on situation awareness, perceived workload, and satisfaction, with significant gains over the LLM-based approach. For psychological ownership, optimized configurations were rated significantly higher than both baselines. Importantly, optimization converged on substantially different configurations across participants, indicating strong individual differences; qualitative findings further explain these personalized outcomes.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: PATHWiSE: Empowering Teachers with a Generative AI Authoring System for Personalized Robot-Assisted Learning.
abstract: Homework assignments often lack the personalized guidance and social interaction crucial for learning. Social robots offer a promising way to bring personalization and interactive support into learning activities; however, teachers rarely have the technical expertise needed to operate robots, let alone create or customize robot-assisted learning (RAL) lessons. To address this challenge, we introduce PATHWiSE, a robust, no-code authoring system designed to empower teachers to create custom RAL activities. Developed through participatory co-design activities with middle school science teachers and students and iteratively refined through multiple user studies, PATHWiSE enables educators to author, preview, and personalize RAL activities that can be tailored to different robot platforms and delivered with either in-person or on-screen robots. The system maintains a flexible trigger-action programming model to define robot expressions contextually related to lesson materials. Through integrated teacher- and student-facing portals, teachers can deploy RAL lessons using a lightweight and portable browser-based approach that affords integration with a wide range of systems. AI-assisted comment and emotion-expression generation tools augment teacher lesson creation while preserving teacher autonomy and expertise in content design. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of PATHWiSE, including its authoring workflow, interface architecture, backend integration, and representative use cases drawn from iterative studies to illustrate the capabilities of the full system.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Be My Ears: Enabling Semantic Alerting for Earphone Wearers with Pheme.
abstract: Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) earphones provide immersive listening experiences but induce auditory isolation to earphone users, leaving them vulnerable to hazards and socially disconnected. We present Pheme , an agentic framework that transforms ANC earphones into context-aware auditory assistants. Informed by two user studies ( N = 385 and N = 34) that reveal a high prevalence of missed critical sounds and significant linguistic ambiguity (73.6%) in user requests, Pheme employs a three-stage pipeline: (1) an LLM-based Query Understanding module to resolve intent and map ambiguous commands to acoustic targets; (2) Text-conditioned Audio Separation (via SAM Audio) to isolate target sounds from ambient noise; and (3) LALM-based Verification to validate detections against user intent, reducing false interruptions. We evaluate Pheme against a baseline that directly feeds ambient audio into an audio language model for target event detection, using 1,584 audio samples across seven real-world scenarios. Our results show that Pheme achieves 82.2% detection accuracy for user-specified audio events at + 5 dB SNR setup, outperforming the baseline by 9.5% while reducing the false positive rate by 11.9%. Moreover, Pheme significantly reduces operational overhead, cutting API calls by 48.1% and LALM audio processing workload by 67.3%.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SketchAloud: Combining Time-Aligned Sketch & Speech for Multimodal Specification of 3D Designs.
abstract: Sketching enables users to quickly express visual ideas. Describing what they are trying to sketch can give generative models additional context for interpreting user intent, but understanding how to combine the sketch and speech data effectively is challenging, particularly when user intent depends on temporal context and deictic references (e.g., “this pillar”). We present SketchAloud, a technique that captures this temporal context by constructing a mapping between speech segments and sketch strokes. We evaluate SketchAloud through two user studies. A controlled experiment (N = 12) examines user interaction, showing that sketch with speech is easier to use and more effective at capturing user intent compared to either modality alone. A follow-up study (N = 700) involving over 35,000 pairwise comparisons assesses output quality, demonstrating that while sketch and speech each offer distinct strengths for specifying structure and semantics, their combination improves both output quality and consistency by reducing failure cases.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Penquiry: A Pen-based Interactive In-situ Q&A System Leveraging LLMs.
abstract: Pen-based digital devices remain a preferred medium for active, cognitively engaging study. Concurrently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have become indispensable for self-directed learning, enabling students to clarify concepts. However, a fundamental interaction gap exists between the fluid, spatial nature of pen-based workflows and the discrete, keyboard-heavy requirements of LLMs. We present Penquiry, an in-situ question-and-answer system that bridges this gap by enabling learners to pose questions directly on digital study materials via a pen. We characterize two primary interaction challenges in this multimodal transition: a Referential Barrier, which hinders grounding fine-grained visual elements into the query context, and an Expressive Barrier, which forces learners to translate diverse, non-textual intents—such as equations and diagrams—into rigid, typed sentences. To resolve these, Penquiry introduces a mediation layer featuring Content Snapping for unambiguous referencing and Question Autocompletion to expand sparse ink keywords into rich semantic queries. Through two iterative user studies (N = 16 per study), we demonstrate that Penquiry significantly reduces the cognitive and physical overhead of inquiry compared to traditional interfaces, providing a new blueprint for pen-based, in-situ AI interaction.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Before You Say It: Anticipating Verbal Behavior from Longitudinal Everyday Conversations with LLMs.
abstract: Knowing someone deeply means not just understanding what they say or do but also how they will likely think, react, and engage across situations. Such predictions could eventually inform systems to anticipate when the individual is about to deviate from their goal, catch regrettable behaviors before they are made, and surface blind spots before they take hold. While many interactive systems model users to enable more personalized interactions, most cannot make such behavioral predictions, as this often requires longitudinal observation and inference of how the individual’s behaviors unfold across various everyday situations. In this work, we introduce a novel LLM-based predictive behavioral modeling approach that anticipates a user’s likely behavior across everyday conversational situations. We (1) collect a longitudinal dataset of over 1,000 hours of naturalistic conversations from 14 participants using a wearable smartwatch; (2) evaluate LLM-based predictions against ground truth behaviors; and (3) use semi-structured interviews to explore participants’ perceptions of behavioral predictions and their views on possible forms of future behavioral support. Altogether, our findings provide evidence that person-specific verbal behavior can be predicted from longitudinal conversational data. This opens up new possibilities for potential future context-aware, anticipatory, proactive and personalized AI systems.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: "What Are You Really Trying to Do?": Co-Creating Life Goals from Everyday Computer Use.
abstract: Recent advances in user modeling make it feasible to conduct open-ended inference over a person’s everyday computer use. Despite longstanding visions of systems that deeply understand our actions and the purposes they serve in our lives, existing systems only capture what a person is doing in the moment, not why they are doing it, limiting these systems to surface-level support. We introduce striving co-creation, a process for inferring broader life goals from unstructured observations of computer use. Grounded in Activity Theory and Emmons’ personal strivings framework, our system progressively constructs a hierarchical representation of a person’s activities. Strivings are, however, difficult to fully resolve from observation alone, as the same action can be driven by many different goals. Our system therefore supports an editing interface that gives people agency over how they are understood by the system, feeding their corrections back into subsequent rounds of striving induction. In a week-long field deployment (N = 14), we find that our co-creation process produces strivings that participants recognize as representative of their long-term goals and gives them greater agency than baseline methods.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Leadership in Human-Robot Teams: Effects of Proactive Agent Behavior on Group Cohesion.
abstract: Hybrid teams of humans and embodied conversational agents (ECAs) are increasingly studied in human–computer interactions to support collaborative activities involving decision-making and coordination. In such settings, effective teamwork relies on positive group dynamics, particularly cohesion, a multidimensional construct reflecting both shared commitment to group tasks and interpersonal bonds among members. Given the established relationship between leadership and cohesion in human teams, this article investigates whether proactive, leader-like ECAs can foster cohesion in hybrid teams. To this end, we design a proactive agent model and adapt a collaborative narration task to support multiple group configurations. We conduct a between-subjects Wizard-of-Oz experiment (N = 64) where teams of two humans and two robots collaborate as peers, comparing a condition where one robot is proactive with a condition where neither robot is. Results validate our agent model and show that groups including a proactive robot report significantly higher task cohesion. Behavioral analyses reveal increased participant involvement. These findings suggest that proactive behaviors inspired by leadership strategies represent a promising design approach for ECAs aiming to foster cohesion in hybrid collaborative settings.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TwistForm: Shaping Reconfigurable 3D Surfaces via Pre-programmed Torsional Deformation of Chains.
abstract: In this paper, we propose TwistForm, a novel shape-forming method that leverages torsion-actuated chains to reconstruct pre-programmed 3D surfaces. By parametrically designing the geometric interlocking of individual ring units, our approach encodes 3D surfaces into continuous, 1D kinematic chains. Upon the application of torsion, these chains undergo a structural phase transition, physically deploying into the pre-programmed 3D shapes. Because this 1D encoding inherently enables significant volumetric compression, TwistForm effectively addresses spatial constraints associated with the transportation and storage of physical objects. To realize this, we developed an end-to-end fabrication framework for designing and physicalizing these chains. Users can utilize this system to import arbitrary 3D models, design the corresponding interlinked chain structures, and export optimized print data for fabrication. We detail the underlying algorithms for unit design and spatial layout, and demonstrate practical use cases, including compact shipping, reusable molds, and shape-changing interfaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SHRIMP: Iterative Refinement of Robot Task Plans.
abstract: As collaborative robots have entered domains such as manufacturing, agriculture, and healthcare, programming or adapting robot behavior typically requires robotic expertise that most end users lack. Natural language lowers this barrier. Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have made it feasible to translate natural language into robot task plans. However, language-based task specification can suffer from semantic ambiguity, and generative models lack transparency for how language instructions are translated into robot actions, making it difficult for users to validate plans before execution. To address these issues, we introduce SHRIMP: Simulation-driven Human-in-the-loop Refinement Interface for Manipulation Planning. SHRIMP allows users to automatically generate a hierarchical robot primitive plan using natural language and iteratively revise their plan through re-prompting and explicit correction. At each revision, SHRIMP allows users to validate their plan in simulation, and once satisfied, execute it on the physical robot. Through a user study involving participants planning tabletop kitchen tasks (N = 35), we validate that SHRIMP improves perceived control and enhances robot transparency. System videos and source code are available at https://wisc-hci.github.io/SHRIMP.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: CapFM: A Foundation Model for Capacitive Touch Sensing.
abstract: Capacitive touch sensing supports rich interactive behavior, yet learning-based methods have been task-specific and rely on labeled datasets that are costly to collect and annotate. We introduce CapFM, a foundation model for capacitive touch sensing that learns a shared representation across diverse touch understanding tasks. We pretrain a Masked Autoencoder on a large corpus of unlabeled capacitive frames across seven datasets, through which our model captures a robust structure in the signal without task-specific supervision. For downstream use, we keep CapFM’s pretrained backbone fixed and attach lightweight task heads that use either global embeddings or spatial token features, depending on task output structure. We evaluate CapFM’s unified approach on eight diverse tasks, including finger identification, pitch and yaw estimation of the finger angle, 3D hand-pose estimation, high-resolution contact area segmentation, and input accuracy. Across these settings, CapFM transfers effectively across datasets and hardware configurations. Using the same training and validation regimen, CapFM pretrained without the respective dataset matches or beats all baselines and shows robust performance. Our results show that foundation-model pretraining makes capacitive sensing models more data-efficient for downstream learning and transferable across tasks and hardware, which can support diverse applications based on CapFM’s pretrained backbone rather than separate task-specific models.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Do Simulated Users Steer Like Humans? A Biomechanical Reinforcement Learning Testbed for Systematic Steering Law Evaluation.
abstract: In interface research, obtaining human performance data remains a persistent bottleneck, which simulated users promise to break. While biomechanical simulation has made significant progress for discrete target acquisition, continuous steering represents a fundamentally harder problem: every UI path geometry imposes different kinematic demands. We present a computational testbed that generates steering trajectories across arbitrary UI paths using a muscle-actuated upper-limb model driven by reinforcement learning, without human reference data and without path-specific redesign. Instantiated across six geometries and six Steering Law formulations, the testbed enables a systematic evaluation of steering performance not just in terms of time, but behavior. Our simulated users adhere to most Steering Law formulations for curved and narrowing path geometries, while L-shaped paths yield weaker fits. A targeted user study (N=12) shows that simulated and human trajectories match in shape on linear, narrowing, circular, and spiral paths, with larger discrepancy for L-shaped and sinusoidal paths. These findings establish biomechanical simulation as a robust computational instrument to study HCI tasks beyond discrete target selections, surfacing conditions that most warrant human investigation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: HueRistic: Optimizing Lighting for Live Video Color Design.
abstract: We present HueRistic, an interactive system that optimizes color in live video through physical lighting control. Our system integrates a camera with programmable LED lights, analyzing the colors in the live feed and measuring the effect of each light source. HueRistic employs closed-loop optimization to find RGB lighting configurations that satisfy specific aesthetic objectives, such as enhancing color harmony or reproducing target colors in the scene. To support rapid exploration, HueRistic includes a design gallery that allows users to compare candidate lighting configurations before applying them to the scene. Our technical evaluation demonstrates that our system accurately simulates and produces high quality lighting solutions that satisfy aesthetic objectives. Our user study finds that HueRistic enables creators to discover lighting parameters that would be challenging to achieve through trial-and-error alone.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Can You Say This for Me? Speaking Up by Proxy in Co-Located Discussion.
abstract: Equal participation in co-located discussion is important for effective collaboration, yet people often hold back when they anticipate negative interpersonal or professional consequences, especially when raising a point requires voicing it themselves. We present SecondVoice, a mixed-reality system that enables people to speak up through an embodied virtual proxy. By separating what is said from who says it, SecondVoice brings hesitant points into the live spoken discussion without putting the speaker on the spot. Using a private overlay, users specify their intent through a structured specification process rather than composing a full utterance. The system reformulates the input and voices it into the conversation through the proxy. We characterize a design space of participation channels under social risk. In a preliminary within-subject study (N = 16), we compare the complete SecondVoice system with an anonymous text-board channel across two group discussion tasks. Half of participants reported using SecondVoice for a point they did not say aloud, compared with 18.8% for the text board. Proxy-delivered points entered the spoken floor and were followed by multi-turn group engagement, which we did not observe after text-board posts. Participants described the channel as situationally valuable but identified tradeoffs around timing, ownership, and trust in reformulation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Earmony: Orchestrating Adaptive Auditory Cardio-Respiratory Biofeedback on Commodity Earables.
abstract: Commodity earbuds are becoming an increasingly promising platform for everyday health and wellness support. Building on their wearability and ubiquity, we present Earmony, an adaptive auditory cardio-respiratory biofeedback system that runs on off-the-shelf earbuds. Using only the built-in in-ear microphone, Earmony unobtrusively senses cardio-respiratory signals without requiring additional sensors. To support simultaneous sensing and audio playback, we develop a robust detection framework that preserves signal quality under concurrent audio output. Building on this capability, we implement a closed-loop system in which auditory feedback is dynamically modulated by the user’s real-time physiological state rather than following a fixed pace. Specifically, musical chords guide breathing and adapt continuously to both breathing dynamics and heart rate variability (HRV), enabling responsive and personalized regulation. A user study (N = 20) shows that Earmony maintains significantly elevated HRV for longer durations than static systems, demonstrating the potential of seamless, earbud-based adaptive biofeedback.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Surpassing Human Wrist Constraints: Dexterity-Enhanced Techniques for Teleoperated Robotic Manipulation.
abstract: Free-hand teleoperation enables intuitive robot control by mapping human hand and arm poses to end-effector motion. However, its effectiveness in complex tasks is constrained by the mismatch between human wrist biomechanics and robotic arm capabilities. From 60 demonstration videos across four task categories, we identified three end-effector motion capabilities that surpass human constraints: unbounded axial rotation, omnidirectional alignment, and path-constrained orientation maintenance. Inspired by enhancement techniques in virtual reality (VR), we propose two interaction strategies—finger-based motion extension and non-isomorphic rotational gain—instantiated in four methods: FingerCircle, FingerRaise, WristSpin, and WristDNR.
