We evaluated these methods in VR using three representative teleoperation tasks, with a clutch-based control mode as the baseline. Results showed that finger-based methods improve efficiency and agency in continuous rotation tasks, whereas wrist-based methods enhance alignment and orientation control, at the expense of predictability. We further deployed them on a UR5 robotic arm in two application scenarios. Overall, these techniques better leverage robotic dexterity while reducing operator workload.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Avatar Cloak: Protecting Behavioral Privacy with State-Aware Motion Substitution in Immersive MR Telepresence.
abstract: Immersive telepresence in Mixed Reality (MR) allows users to communicate through embodied avatars driven by live-tracked motion. While this supports embodied interaction, it can also expose privacy-sensitive behaviors. This creates a gap between protecting behavioral privacy and maintaining interaction quality. To address this, we present Avatar Cloak, a motion substitution concept that replaces live-tracked motion with appropriate animations to conceal sensitive behaviors. Through a formative study, we implemented a State-Aware Substitution that substitutes avatar motion based on conversational states when users choose to conceal behaviors. A user study (N=36) showed that State-Aware Substitution increased users’ sense of control over privacy, reduced concerns about misinterpretation, and enhanced engagement and message understanding. These findings inform future designs of motion substitution systems for balancing privacy protection with embodied interaction in MR telepresence.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: EcoVibWood: Lower Impact Vibration Sensing in Plywood.
abstract: In this paper, we present EcoVibWood, an approach that combines alternative sensing materials with an automatic protective mechanism to support lower-impact plywood vibration sensing. We systematically explore commercially available alternatives for the triboelectric and electrode layers, including zinc, iron, gold leaf, graphite, paper, PBAT, and PLA, and evaluate whether they can retain the sensing performance of conventional copper and PTFE configurations. We further introduce a protective mechanism made from wood and bamboo that automatically isolates affected electrodes when screws penetrate the plywood, without requiring electronic components or manual intervention. Our experiments show that several alternative layer combinations achieve signal strength and SNRs comparable to, or exceeding, those of traditional copper–PTFE configurations. We integrate these materials into a working prototype and evaluate its performance across 26 everyday activities. EcoVibWood achieves an average recognition accuracy of 83.3% using a Random Forest classifier and 94.7% using a convolutional neural network, demonstrating that lower-impact material substitutions can support robust activity recognition.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ExtenString: Enhancing String-Based Interaction with Virtual Screens through Remapping.
abstract: Previous research has investigated string-based systems that bridge the fingertips and head-mounted displays (HMDs) to provide physical support when users reach out to click in virtual reality (VR). These systems rely only on a low-cost, simple passive string and have demonstrated exemplary performance. However, the limited hand movement range may restrict interaction space. We explored the use of remapping to overcome interaction in physical constraints, thereby supporting a wider range of scenarios. While users move on the spherical surface defined by the string, interactions can be mapped to virtual screens with positions and sizes different from the physical layout. We conducted studies to identify optimized designs that enhance user performance and satisfaction across various screen usage contexts, including physical interaction positions and cross-screen tasks. Finally, we demonstrate how the proposed method enables various scenarios in applications and discuss its potential use cases.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: FontCopilot: A Designer-in-the-Loop System for Chinese Vector Font Design.
abstract: Designing Chinese fonts is challenging due to the structural complexity of ideographic characters and the scale of character sets (e.g., over 80,000 characters in GB 18030). Existing font generation methods often produce non-editable raster images or offer limited stylistic control, which restricts their use in professional design workflows. We present FontCopilot, an interactive designer-in-the-loop system for Chinese vector font design. Through an exploratory interview study with 10 professional designers, we identify Component Assembly as a major production bottleneck. FontCopilot targets this labor-intensive phase using a component-based affine transformation model that generates editable vector glyphs from few-shot inputs. The workflow lets designers refine generated results and use their corrections to update the model. These interactions provide direct control over component layout and style. We evaluate CAR through model ablations and a comparison with a prior Chinese vector font generation method, study FontCopilot with 9 professional designers, and document a four-week production case. FontCopilot received “Excellent” ratings on five of six UEQ dimensions, and one designer used 300 seed characters to produce 10,461 editable glyphs for AI Song . Together, these evaluations show how editable component completion can carry local structural decisions from a small seed set to a complete Chinese typeface.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Predicting Tool Extension in VR Interactions Using Gaze Features.
abstract: The ability for virtual reality (VR) systems to create a sense of presence in users has long captured the attention of HCI researchers. One aspect of presence during interaction is tool extension - the experience of integrating a tool into one’s body schema. Prior research shows that features of visual attention correlate with experiencing tool extension in VR, but no previous methods provide an ability to predict a user’s tool extension state in real-time. We investigate building this predictor through a study with 18 participants. Participants used virtual tools designed to either promote or inhibit tool extension (a simple hammer vs. an unpredictable linkage-driven hammer). VR gaze-tracking data reliably distinguished these conditions based on the distribution of gaze across areas of interest such as tool, task, and elsewhere. We also found that perspective (first vs. third person) did not affect tool extension. Our results suggest a straightforward gaze-based predictor for tool extension. We conclude by providing a design space demonstrating the practical value of this predictor and several applications enabled by it.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: AtmoSteer: Personalized Scene Control with Reusable Atmospheric Recipes.
abstract: Generating scenes that convey atmospheres such as “cozy” or “contemplative” is difficult because people interpret them subjectively and often struggle to express them concretely. We present AtmoSteer, a human-in-the-loop approach that captures a user’s personal interpretation of an atmosphere as an atmospheric recipe: a weighted set of descriptive tags that can be reused across scenes for tasks such as image generation and image search. AtmoSteer supports users in discovering their own atmospheric recipes by exploring diverse interpretations with images and constructing a personalized vocabulary of visually grounded tags that describe style, layout, objects, and lighting. The system then supports preference refinement through two modes: slider-based weight adjustment of tags and visual example-based elicitation. In a user study on image generation (N=20), images generated from recipes produced by AtmoSteer were significantly more preferred and better aligned with participants’ subjective interpretations than those generated using generic descriptors or style transfer techniques.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MuTable: Composable and Reusable Table Transformations for In-Situ Data Exploration.
abstract: Tables are central to data work to support precise lookup and full detail, but they can be limiting for overview and pattern-finding tasks. Visualizations are then created to gain richer perceptual support. In practice, moving between tables and charts often requires maintaining parallel representations, introducing context switching, and extra coordination work. Building on prior hybrid table-visualization systems, we present MuTable, a prototype that reifies transformations as persistent, composable, and reusable modifiers to support in-situ data exploration. Users can reshape the table while retaining and adapting intermediate forms as their questions evolve. An expert interview with eight data workers suggests that MuTable can support coordination between representations, rapid exploration, and greater user agency in constructing visualizations, as a low-commitment exploration space.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TalkEase: A Multimodal Personalized Topic Guidance System for Long-distance Couples' Video Calls Driven by LLM.
abstract: Video-mediated communication (VMC) is vital for long-distance couples, yet the lack of shared context often leads to conversational stagnation. We present TalkEase, a real-time multimodal conversational support system that alleviates topic exhaustion through a sensing-understanding-action loop. TalkEase integrates multimodal interaction cues, including conversational rhythm, turn-taking dynamics, and affect-related signals, to estimate potential moments of interactional difficulty and provide contextualized topic suggestions. We introduce non-intrusive interaction techniques: “Topic Bubbles” provide shared peripheral visual anchors, while a “Shuffle” function empowers users with agency over AI suggestions. We further present Adaptive Fading, a theory-informed artifact mechanism inspired by scaffolding principles, which explores how AI assistance may gradually recede as users develop greater conversational autonomy. A mixed-methods study with 60 long-distance couples shows that TalkEase improves immediate Perceived Partner Responsiveness (PPR) and shifts cognitive demand from high-pressure topic generation toward low-stress suggestion evaluation. Our work offers an empirically grounded interaction approach for AI-assisted intimate communication while establishing design directions for future adaptive conversational support.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: VeriForge: Mitigating Latent Knowledge Gaps in Narrative Drafting via Mixed-Initiative Scaffolding.
abstract: Great fiction earns its verisimilitude through precise details, from how a longsword is gripped to pierce armor gaps to why a bleeding corpse cannot yet smell of decay, weaving domain expertise into the fabric of invented worlds. Current AI writing tools offer limited support for discovering and integrating unfamiliar domain knowledge into narrative. They require explicit queries that authors cannot formulate, generate finished prose that risks homogenizing voice, or assist only within the boundaries of what authors already know. We argue that AI should reveal latent knowledge gaps to writers while preserving their agency to transform discovered knowledge into authentic prose. Grounded in formative interviews with 9 fiction writers, we present VeriForge, a mixed-initiative writing system that divides cognitive labor so that the system assumes initiative over domain discovery while the author retains full initiative over narrative synthesis. VeriForge realizes this through three complementary mechanisms. Proactive inline highlighting flags potential knowledge gaps as authors draft. Dual-stream querying pairs conversational responses with source-anchored Knowledge Cards for direct fact extraction. A spatial Knowledge Canvas allows authors to organize and connect discovered knowledge across their writing. These mechanisms are powered by a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation pipeline grounded in domain-specific source materials. A within-subjects user study (N=12) provides preliminary evidence that this paradigm helps authors recognize previously overlooked knowledge gaps, supports creative exploration, and is perceived by expert raters to produce passages with stronger domain grounding in a controlled cold-start writing task.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: TailorCoPilot: Enabling Agentic Pattern Making with Version-Controlled State Tracking.
abstract: Experience-driven manufacturing, such as garment pattern making, faces a severe generational skills gap because its core expertise relies on undocumented tacit knowledge forged through day-to-day practice. To address this challenge, we present TailorCoPilot, an agentic pattern-making system built upon a specially designed version-control backend TailorTrace. TailorTrace models sewing patterns as structured, discrete states and records their transformations during the pattern-making process as explicit operation sequences defined upon the geometry primitives in the sewing pattern (panels, edges, vertices and stitches). Integrated into a conventional pattern-making GUI, TailorTrace enables seamless documentation of senior experts’ tacit pattern-making knowledge without breaking their daily workflow. The documented knowledge further offers interactive, pedagogical scaffolding for novices, while providing a robust foundation to power TailorCoPilot and train future generative AI models. In a user study with novices and advanced novices, TailorCoPilot improved task completion rates, reduced time and perceived workload, and yielded higher-quality artifacts compared to skill-appropriate baselines. Ultimately, TailorCoPilot demonstrates a viable pathway to capture practice-based expertise, operationalizing it to support both generative AI advancements and human apprenticeship.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MuscleJockey: Motor Initiation via Electrical Muscle Stimulation While Preserving User Control.
abstract: In body-actuation interfaces, due to the difficulty predicting user intention in real time, it is challenging to induce movements while preserving user control. We propose MuscleJockey, a body-actuation interface concept in which the system controls the initiation of a movement, while the user controls the direction of the movement. MuscleJockey is based on the division of roles between machine and human: electrical muscle stimulation applied to the shoulder initiates the movement, while the user handles this initiated movement to reach toward a prepared direction. We conducted a user study in which cues were presented at random times, and participants performed reaching movements toward the direction that had been presented beforehand. Consequently, MuscleJockey resulted in a significantly shorter time from cue to movement onset (63.0 ms shorter than the control condition), while maintaining comparable directional accuracy across conditions. These results provide evidence that the time between cue and movement onset can be reduced while preserving user control. Future work should evaluate user control in precise direction, force, and pointing tasks. We believe this study opens up an alternative design direction for body-actuation interfaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SnowEcho: End-to-End Blind Skiing Assistance System Using Spatial Audio for Simulated Dynamic Slope.
abstract: Blind skiing usually relies on a sighted guide, limiting opportunities for independent participation. Prior ski assistance systems mainly use route guidance and assume static obstacles or ideal sensing, making them less suitable for crowded, dynamic slopes. We present SnowEcho, a skiing assistance system for people with visual impairments (PVI) that uses spatial audio to convey obstacle direction and distance, allowing skiers to choose their own line. In a simulator study with visually impaired skiers, SnowEcho improved obstacle avoidance and increased clearance in dense dynamic environments compared with a route-guidance baseline, while also improving perceived independence and consistency. We further tested an end-to-end sensing pipeline with depth-based detection and segmentation. Performance remained close to simulator ground truth conditions under moderate noise, but severe noise reduced clearance, confidence, and feedback consistency. These findings indicate both the promise of spatial audio scene awareness and the importance of cue stability under realistic sensing noise.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Present Drawing: Exploring Avatar-Mediated Drawing Events with Physical Traces.
abstract: We introduce Present Drawing, an approach for staging an avatar-mediated drawing event that leaves physical traces in the real world. Present Drawing aims to reconfigure conventional drawing events by relaxing their physical constraints. We describe an organizer-oriented design space for such an event along four elements: Time, Site, Control Source, and Avatar Embodiment. To ground this concept, we developed a proof-of-concept prototype in which an observer wears a head-mounted display to view an avatar. The avatar’s motion is synchronized with a customized pen plotter whose mechanical parts are hidden from the observer. We also developed five application examples spanning live, playback, multi-site, mascot, and system-controlled configurations. We conducted an initial evaluation of one representative playback autograph configuration, showing the basic plausibility of the core Present Drawing experience as an avatar-mediated drawing event and highlighting factors associated with perceiving the avatar as the drawer.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: NaturalEdit: Code Modification through Direct Interaction with Adaptive Natural Language Representation.
abstract: Code modification requires developers to comprehend code, plan changes, articulate intent, and validate outcomes, making it cognitively demanding. While natural language (NL) code summaries offer a promising external representation of this process, existing approaches remain limited. Systems grounded in exploratory data analysis are restricted to narrow domains, while general-purpose systems enforce fixed NL representations and assume that developers can directly translate vague intent into precise textual edits. We present NaturalEdit, which treats code summaries as interactive representations tightly linked to source code. Grounded in the Cognitive Dimensions of Notations, NaturalEdit introduces three key features: (1) adaptive, multi-faceted code summaries with a flexible Abstraction Gradient; (2) interactive mapping mechanisms between summaries and code that ensure tight, structurally stable Closeness of Mapping; and (3) intent-driven bidirectional synchronization that reduces Viscosity during editing while preserving Visibility and Consistency through incremental diffs. A technical evaluation confirms NaturalEdit’s viability, and a user study with 20 developers shows that it improves comprehension, intent articulation, and validation while increasing developers’ perceived confidence and control.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Data-Oriented Debugging Across Place and Time.
abstract: Programmers routinely instrument and run their code with tools such as print statements or breakpoints in order to understand how their programs behave at runtime. When multiple tools are available to programmers, how should we think about their strengths and weaknesses? In this paper, we provide one lens for comparison called data-oriented debugging. In this lens, a programmer has data needs and expresses them as queries to their debugging tools. Queries reach into clusters of program data organized by place and time. Tools differ in which of these queries they make easy. We develop this lens through formative interviews with professional programmers, a comparative tool-use study, and an analysis of existing debugging tools. We offer the lens as a reflective aid for tool designers and researchers to assess the capabilities of a debugging tool of interest.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Reperceiving Everyday Sounds with Hidden Texture.
abstract: Ubiquitous hearable devices often prioritize digital immersion by suppressing real-world sounds, distancing users from their physical surroundings. Conversely, noticing rich acoustic details in everyday sounds brings benefits such as supporting mindfulness and fostering musical appreciation. We explore how hearables can scaffold users to hear “more” of their everyday soundscapes. We present a wearable system that identifies hidden textures in everyday sounds, specifically overtones that shape timbre but are often perceptually hidden. Grounded in prior literature in auditory cueing, the system amplifies these overlooked textures in real time to produce a short-term attentional shift, enabling users to continue noticing these details after device use. We evaluated the system through two studies. A psychoacoustic study (n = 32) showed that the overtone textures detected by our system could be effectively cued. Across 10 sounds, participants showed a 13% improvement in detecting the overtone texture immediately after one-time cueing. These results were further validated by an in-lab user study (n = 12), where participants wore the system while interacting with everyday objects. In 69% of trials, participants reported that cued texture became more perceptually salient after using the device than before. Qualitative accounts further suggested that the device use could encourage participants to form new mental associations with familiar sounds.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Exhale to Execute: Transforming Commercial Microphone Arrays into Directional Airflow Sensors for Ubiquitous Interaction.
abstract: Ubiquitous computing environments frequently require hands-free input methods when users are physically occupied. Current exhalation detection approaches rely on dedicated airflow sensors or utilize standard microphones with basic volume thresholds. We introduce a software framework designed to repurpose commercial microphone arrays for directional airflow sensing. To address the limitations of simple amplitude thresholds, our system employs an absolute-energy gate, a cross-channel energy-uniformity ratio, and non-linear energy-weighted mapping. This acoustic pipeline enables standard microphones to estimate airflow direction under controlled conditions. Technical evaluations with a calibrated mechanical airflow source show that the framework distinguishes localized airflow impacts from the tested far-field background noise and separates coarse directional targets. This work includes no human-subject evaluation; the interactive demonstrations illustrate proof-of-concept mappings rather than validated interaction performance.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film.
abstract: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character’s reactions to important moments. These small, detailed edits are slow and tedious to make in standard editing tools because users have to map high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame adjustments. At the same time, these fine-scale adjustments, which we call micro-edits, can be nuanced and expressive, with different choices serving different creative goals. In this work, we start by conducting a formative study with professional editors to understand the structure of micro-edits and how they are used. We then derive a mathematical formalization for this structure to develop tools that leverage AI and optimization to make exploring micro-edits simpler and more efficient for users. Finally, we validate our tools in multiple user studies and a wide range of video examples.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Hear-to-Hear: Uncertainty-Aware, Head-Tracked Interaction for Personalized Spatial Audio.
abstract: Selecting a personalized head-related transfer function (HRTF) is essential for accurate spatial audio, but remains challenging due to substantial user variation and noisy subjective feedback. We present a real-time, uncertainty-aware perceptual interaction loop for HRTF personalization: after each paired comparison, the system updates a posterior belief over candidate HRTFs and immediately adapts the next query to maximize informativeness. Our system couples Bayesian preference learning with real-time head-tracked binaural rendering, enabling head motion to actively inform comparisons. In a controlled within-subject psychophysical study, uncertainty-aware interaction (with optional head tracking) provides directional posterior evidence for localization improvements—primarily suggestive reductions in azimuth error and front–back confusions concentrated in the front hemisphere—alongside participant-level heterogeneity and a partially mitigated elevation trade-off, rather than uniformly decisive effects across all metrics.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI.
abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200–600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) structured knowledge analysis with multi-modal understanding to ensure pedagogical rigor; (2) a two-stage generate-verify-optimize pipeline separating content alignment from visual refinement; and (3) Click-to-Locate editing with Unified Diff-based incremental generation achieving sub-10-second iteration cycles. A controlled lab study with 40 participants shows MAIC-UI reduces editing iterations (4.9 vs. 7.0) and significantly improves learnability and controllability compared to direct Text-to-HTML generation. A three-month classroom deployment with 53 high school students demonstrates that MAIC-UI fosters learning agency and reduces outcome disparities—the pilot class achieved 9.21-point gains in STEM subjects compared to -2.32 points in control classes. Our code is available at https://github.com/THU-MAIC/MAIC-UI.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SplatXR: A Toolkit for Multi-Layered Extended Reality via On-Headset 3D Gaussian Splatting.
abstract: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting, 3D foundation models, and video-passthrough mixed reality offer unprecedented fidelity for capturing and blending physical and virtual worlds. However, established XR methods rely on polygon-based pipelines that treat physical and digital environments as separate domains, making seamless integration across recent novel representations difficult. Because splats lack explicit surface geometry, they impede standard graphics techniques necessary for cross-reality interactions, such as shadow or collision handling. Furthermore, while 3D foundation models can reconstruct physical objects on-the-fly into digital splats, current XR systems fall short of leveraging this capability for user experiences that transition seamlessly between physicality and virtuality. To address this, we organize XR as a multi-layered reality of interacting primitives, letting pixels and objects move across physical and digital boundaries. We contribute SplatXR, a Unity toolkit that operationalizes this structure as building blocks for interactive, immersive apps leveraging 3D Gaussian splatting: a standalone renderer, splat-to-mesh reconstruction, splat physics, splat blending, and offloaded splat object reconstruction via on-headset capture. SplatXR unites vision and graphics techniques to make splat-based XR development broadly available, and we validate it through demonstrative applications and a small developer study.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Faster Than Muscle: Executing Action based on Voluntary Nervous Signals.
abstract: Human augmentation enables actions that surpass biological limits, but earlier intervention in the action loop can undermine user agency. We introduce human-in-the-loop action acceleration, a design approach that anchors action acceleration to voluntary initiation. Using forearm EMG onset, the system triggers actuation within the electromechanical delay (EMD), enabling earlier execution without relying on predictive inference. We implement this approach in Faster Than Muscle, a system with three instantiations: (1) on-body finger actuation achieving a 51 ms speedup, (2) EMG-triggered software input for a shooting task (82 ms speedup), and (3) bionic-hand actuation for catching a falling object (19 ms speedup). Across two studies (temporal binding experiment and qualitative interview study) and accompanying system evaluations, we show that EMG-triggered acceleration improves performance in time-critical tasks, while users retain a sense of agency. These results show that actions can be accelerated beyond biological limits while remaining grounded in voluntary initiation, and outline a design space spanning execution targets and feedback timing.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Mirror Skin: In Situ Visualization of Robot Touch Intent on Robot Skin.
abstract: Effective communication of robot touch intent is essential for safe and predictable physical human-robot interaction. While intent communication has been widely studied, existing approaches lack the spatial specificity and semantic depth necessary to efficiently convey robot touch intent. We present Mirror Skin, a cephalopod-inspired concept that mirrors in-situ visual representations of a human’s body parts onto the corresponding robot’s touch region to communicate who shall initiate touch, where it will occur, and when it is imminent. We informed the design of Mirror Skin through a structured design exploration with experts and demonstrate the real-world feasibility of Mirror Skin with a proof-of-concept prototype. User studies in VR and with the physical prototype showed that Mirror Skin significantly improves accuracy and response times for interpreting touch intent and improves the user experience during physical human-robot interactions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SiMUSation: An Interactive Visitor Experience Simulation Framework to Support Museum Exhibition Design.
abstract: Understanding how diverse audiences engage with narratives and content is central to exhibition design, yet designers often rely on intuition. Existing experience evaluation methods are typically retrospective, costly, and offer limited access to visitors’ internal states, hindering early-stage iterative refinement. Rather than relying only on post-implementation evaluation with real visitors, we explore LLM-driven persona simulation as a reference for early-stage design. Following this idea, we present SiMUSation, an interactive framework designed to support early-stage exhibition design. SiMUSation models diverse visitor personas and simulates their exhibition experiences through a dual-layer representation that couples observable behaviors, such as movement and gaze, with corresponding internal responses, such as confusion and narrative engagement. Designers can steer simulations, inspect feedback from simulated visits, and iteratively revise layouts, content, and narrative flow to further examine how changes reshape visitor experience. We implemented a prototype and evaluated it through a user study (N=12), showing that SiMUSation provides insights for reflection and refinement in early-stage exhibition design. Our findings further highlight the potential of persona-driven simulation to support audience-informed evaluation and iterative decision-making across design tasks.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Granular I/O: Enabling Bi-directional Malleable Interaction for Actuated TUIs with Magnetic Particles.
abstract: Granular materials — clusters of small discrete particles — afford a uniquely malleable form of physical interaction, enabling intuitive shaping, splitting, and merging through natural hand gestures. Despite their rich interaction potential, granular materials remain largely unexplored as a form factor for actuated, bi-directional Tangible User Interfaces (TUIs). We present Granular I/O, an approach that employs millimeter-scale passive magnetic particle clusters, actuated by external magnetic field controllers, to enable malleable input and output interactions for granular-based actuated TUIs. We describe a comprehensive design space for malleable granular interaction, alongside a full hardware and software implementation covering particle cluster fabrication, two actuation platforms, and authoring software. We further report technical characterization and evaluation to validate the system, and demonstrate a range of applications that harness malleable I/O for interactive use.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Elsewise: Authoring Open-ended Interactive Narrative with Possibility Space Visualization.
abstract: Interactive narrative (IN) authors craft spaces of divergent narrative possibilities for players to explore, with the player’s input determining which narrative possibilities they actually experience. Generative AI can enable new forms of IN by improvisationally expanding on pre-authored content in response to open-ended player input. However, this extrapolation risks widening the gap between author-envisioned and player-experienced stories, potentially limiting the strength of plot progression and the communication of the author’s narrative intent. To bridge the gap, we introduce Elsewise: an authoring tool for LLM-based INs that implements a novel Bundled Storyline concept to enhance authors’ perception and understanding of the narrative possibility space, allowing authors to explore similarities and differences between possible playthroughs of their IN in terms of open-ended, user-configurable narrative dimensions. A user study (n=12) shows that our approach improves author anticipation of player-experienced narrative, leading to more effective control and exploration of narrative possibility spaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MultiVerse: A Creator-Centered Approach to Steering Context-Adaptive Lyrics.
abstract: Generative AI may enable new forms of context-aware creative expression by dynamically tailoring media content to its consumption context. For instance, AI systems could adapt song lyrics to the listener and their current activity. However, existing media adaptation systems primarily optimize for audience experience, often neglecting artists’ intent, style, and preference. We address this challenge by introducing a novel creator-centered approach to adaptive media authoring and present MultiVerse, a system that instantiates this approach for steering adaptive lyrics. Our approach allows creators to explicitly author controls based on their intent, lyric structure, and audience context, and uses rule-based validations to ensure controls are followed. We conducted a study with 10 songwriters, comparing MultiVerse with a prompting-based workflow for composing adaptive lyrics. The comparison revealed that creators preferred to author how lyrics adapt by explicitly specifying relevant context and adaptation constraints, while recognizing trade-offs in flexibility and iteration speed. Interviews further revealed that creators viewed adaptive media as enabling new forms of audience connection, introducing a distinct creative process, favoring new compositional strategies, and reshaping notions of authorship.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SemanticSlider3D: Training-Free Continuous Semantic Editing for 3D Objects.
abstract: Fine-grained control over continuous semantic attributes of 3D objects is essential for 3D content creation, but is not well supported by conventional 3D modeling workflows or prompt-based interaction with existing generative AI tools. While slider-based methods have proven effective for fine-grained semantic control in 2D image generation, no equivalent approach exists for 3D. Extending these 2D methods to 3D is non-trivial due to challenges unique to 3D, including geometric integrity and cross-view coherence. We present SemanticSlider3D, a technique for continuous semantic attribute editing of 3D objects that requires no per-attribute training. Given a user-specified attribute, our pipeline constructs a semantic editing direction in the latent space of a state-of-the-art 3D generation model, presenting a diverse and coherent spectrum of 3D variations. A technical validation on a dataset of 50 3D object-attribute pairs shows our method was preferred by all five human assessors across variation range, consistency, 3D object quality, and attribute disentanglement, over a baseline combining a 2D slider with an image-to-3D model. An exploratory study with six participants demonstrates that SemanticSlider3D supported decision-making in 3D prototyping and was perceived as a valuable addition to existing workflows.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SilkSense: A Craft-Inspired Fabrication Method for Silk-based Functional Interfaces.
abstract: While silk is attractive for on-body sensing due to its biocompatibility and skin affinity, its smooth fiber surface and limited capillary absorption make it poorly suited to existing fabrication methods based on liquid infiltration and mechanical anchoring. Inspired by Gambiered Canton Gauze (Xiangyunsha), a traditional craft with a centuries-long history of silk surface modification, we present SilkSense, a fabric-level workflow for functionalizing commercially available silk. By analyzing the craft’s core processing stages and identifying the underlying interfacial mechanisms, we organize the responsible material components into a two-stage workflow: Dioscorea cirrhosa polyphenol pretreatment followed by Fe-HA/FA and PEDOT: PSS composite coating. The resulting fabric supports mask-based patterning (up to 1.5 mm resolution) and freehand painting and exhibits wash durability (approximately 15.6% resistance drift after 20 high-intensity cycles) under our test conditions. SilkSense fabric enables three on-body input modalities, including pressing, bending, and pinching, whose sensing characteristics can be translated into wearable interface designs across different body locations, validated through a drone control demonstration in which subtle single-hand finger movements drive three-channel real-time closed-loop interaction. Together, these results show how craft-derived interfacial principles can support patternable, maintainable, and multimodal silk-based interaction surfaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: From Style Replication to Style Exploration: Enabling Art Style Exploration with Analyze-Experiment-Resituate Framework.
abstract: Art style is a signature of professional digital artists that develops through repeated experimentation, reflection, and adaptation. While generative AI (GenAI) can reproduce styles with high fidelity, current tools provide limited support for exploring new stylistic directions and may encourage style replication over exploration. To address this gap, we propose Analyze-Experiment-Resituate (AER), a framework for AI-assisted style exploration derived from interviews with 10 professional digital artists. Rather than prioritizing visually appealing outputs alone, AER supports three core practices of style exploration, including interpreting references, trying out stylistic possibilities, and reflecting on how emerging styles may be received. Specifically, AER enabled artists to (1) analyze artworks into interpretable stylistic elements, (2) have controllable experimentation guided by their own choices, and (3) resituate emerging styles through simulated social perspectives. We implemented AER in a prototype system and evaluated it in a controlled study with 16 artists. Compared with a direct style-transfer workflow, AER increased artists’ agency and reflection as they pursued new stylistic directions. A two-week field study with four artists revealed how the AER framework influenced daily style exploration, such as reflection, experimentation, and stylistic decision-making at each stage. We discuss opportunities and challenges in designing AI-assisted style-exploration workflows, and outline implications for future artistic support tools.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Kneadix: A Multi-Process Loom with Dynamic Warp-Weft Role Assignment.
abstract: Current weaving technology permanently sets the role of the warp and weft yarns during the setup phase of production. This limitation is inherent to the structure of modern looms in which the warp actuation mechanism (heddle) commits the layout before fabrication starts. In this paper, we propose a heddle-less loom architecture in which yarn carriers are manipulated by a set of horn gears, an actuation mechanism adapted from braiding machines [47]. By re-interpreting weaving, knitting, and braiding as yarn-twisting processes, we demonstrate that our design can create fabrics combining these processes without seams. We present a proof-of-concept implementation illustrating actuation, yarn tension management, and combing. We used this implementation to validate our design by fabricating fabrics that combine all three processes, manage yarn insertion, and handle complex edge management. We conclude with a discussion of the limitations of the current prototype and its potential beyond a flat sheet of fabric.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Graphionale: How Graph Visualizations of LLM Rationales Affect Human Decision Making.
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly equipped with augmented reasoning capabilities to generate rationales that support human decision-making. Yet these text-dense rationales often impose substantial cognitive burdens. Building on a formative co-design study that identified user preferences for non-linear reasoning representations, we developed Graphionale as a testbed for empirically studying argument-map-style rationale visualization. This system transforms linear LLM rationales into interactive, multi-level graphs. It explicitly structures logical relationships (e.g., conclusions, premises, support, and objections), while further extracting entities and relations within each statement to construct condensed node-link representations. We conduct a large-scale online user study (N = 204) to examine when graphical rationales are more effective than textual ones, across varying task modality (verbal vs. visual reasoning), rationale format (textual vs. graphical), and question difficulty (easy vs. hard). Our results show that graphical rationales do not help uniformly: they improve trust calibration for verbal reasoning yet feel more cognitively demanding and less satisfying; for visual reasoning, they impair calibration yet feel more engaging and helpful. In each modality, the format that better supports calibrated decisions is not the one users prefer, highlighting that matching rationale format to task modality is key to effective AI explanation design. Our findings contribute empirical design knowledge about when and how graphical rationales support human decision making, and inform the next-generation reasoning-aware AI interfaces.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: 4DOrthosis: Therapist-in-the-Loop Design and Fabrication of Force-Customized Hand Orthoses via 4D Printing.
abstract: Hand orthoses play an important role in rehabilitation by stabilizing joints and facilitating movement, with progressive resistance training being particularly critical for muscle function recovery. Yet existing fabrication workflows rarely support patient-specific fit, force customization, and workflow-compatible monitoring simultaneously. We developed 4DOrthosis through a therapist-in-the-loop process that elicited three design requirements: personalized force, efficient fabrication, and support for monitoring-enabled rehabilitation workflows. 4DOrthosis combines FDM-based 4D printing, a force-structure characterization pipeline, and a parametric design tool that generates orthoses from patient hand dimensions and target force requirements, achieving customized rehabilitative force within an experimentally characterized range of 1–20 N. Studies with five rehabilitation-related evaluators and six users indicate feasibility, workflow compatibility, positioning 4DOrthosis as a practical human-centered fabrication approach for rehabilitation devices.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: V-Hook: Morphology-Mediated Vibration-Driven Locomotion through 3D-Printed Hook Structures.
abstract: Vibration is a lightweight and widely available actuation source, yet existing vibration-driven locomotion systems often rely on specialized mechanisms, additional electronics, or extensive empirical tuning, making them difficult to reproduce, adapt, and integrate into everyday objects. To address this limitation, we present V-Hook, a morphology-mediated locomotion design approach that biases motion behavior through hook-shaped structures fabricated by FDM 3D printing. By leveraging asymmetric contact and stick-slip interactions between the hooks and the supporting surface, V-Hook transforms simple vibration input into distinguishable motion tendencies under specific contact and excitation conditions. We systematically investigate how hook forms, array configurations, lengths, and vibration conditions influence motion directional accuracy, stability, and load-bearing performance, and explore a design space of morphology-mediated locomotion from these results. Building on this foundation, we develop a guided design software and online platform that support morphological fabrication and sharing for lightweight interactive objects, and demonstrate the approach through a series of application prototypes. By reframing vibration-driven locomotion as a problem of hook morphology design, this work offers a new perspective for integrating motion capabilities into digitally fabricated interactive systems.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MagicPen: Enabling Dynamic Physical Scaffolding through Haptic Feedback for 3D Content Creation in VR with a Variable-length Stylus.
abstract: Stylus interaction is widely used for 3D content creation. In VR, it is typically mid-air, offering spatial freedom while lacking the grounded haptic feedback required for both shape perception and active geometric editing. To address this, we present MagicPen, a variable-length stylus that delivers grounded haptic feedback and enables active 3D editing through on-surface interaction. MagicPen operates through dynamic physical scaffolding, an interaction approach that adjusts the length to the interaction context: compliantly rendering geometry the user is actively creating, or resistively rendering predefined virtual geometry as a rigid constraint. We conducted three user studies comparing MagicPen with mid-air interaction in terms of accuracy, task load, and user preference: (1) single-axis positioning for depth precision; (2) freeform 3D planar drawing in compliant mode; and (3) drawing on rendered geometry in rigid mode. Results show MagicPen improves depth positioning. MagicPen better supports 3D content creation by enabling grounded shape perception.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: ATOM: Geometry-Aware Microgesture towards Object-Agnostic Tangible Interaction.
abstract: This paper presents ATOM, an integrated framework towards agnostic and tangible object interactions with microgestures. Our goal is to support microgesture interactions across different everyday objects, with the capability to automatically leverage the geometric affordance of each object. We formulate a fingertip-aware detection pipeline to leverage generative 2D and 3D models for geometry enhancement and refinement. We then introduce a usability-based method to prioritize the detected elements based on their ergonomic suitability for interactions. Building on this foundation, we further develop an AR system to transform everyday handheld objects into tangible user interfaces with 0D, 1D, and 2D microgesture interactions. Across transitions among everyday cooking objects of varying shapes and sizes, ATOM outperformed ablation baselines in task completion, usability (SUS), and workload (NASA-TLX). A further study with 10 objects demonstrates ATOM’s generalizability across objects and grasps, highlighting its potential towards fluid, object-agnostic tangible interaction in real-world AR scenarios.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: While You're Still Busy: Context-Aware Approach Optimization for Proactive Mobile Robots.
abstract: Robot assistants are increasingly capable of assisting users in everyday environments, yet they don’t take users’ cognitive context into consideration. As a result, proactive behaviors may interrupt users during cognitively demanding tasks, before they can acknowledge or respond. We identify this pre-acknowledgment window as a critical phase and introduce our real-time optimization approach that adapts how robots approach and communicate during this window, using user engagement signals and task context. Our system jointly optimizes movement and speech by solving structured, closed-form quadratic subproblems that balance disturbance, clarity, and efficiency online. This enables continuous adjustment of approach movement, timing of intent expression, and level of detail without explicit user input. In a within-subjects ablation user study (N = 12), we find that adapting speech to context improves intent clarity, that speed adaptation alone has limited impact without paired speech adaptation, and that coordinating both channels yields the strongest animacy. We also demonstrate the real-world application in three everyday scenarios.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Training Under Pressure: Designing and Evaluating a Multi-Stressor VR Environment for Public Speaking Training.
abstract: Effective public speaking requires performing under stress, yet prior VR training systems have primarily focused on reducing anxiety rather than building the resilience to withstand it. In this paper, we introduce a multi-stressor VR public speaking training system that combines audience non-verbal behavior, crowd size, and AI-generated contextual Q&A, each designed across manipulable levels of stress. In an exploratory within-subjects study (N = 12), we characterize how combined stressor intensity relates to speaking performance and the contribution of individual stressors. Results show that our parameterized stressor design successfully induced distinct anxiety levels, with negative non-verbal animations serving as a stronger source of stress than either crowd size or AI-generated adversarial interruptions. In addition, AI interruptions forced a cognitive context switch during speech, prompting speakers to adopt coping strategies such as adjusting eye gaze and pacing to regain composure. Finally, participants identified the high-stress negative audience condition as the most valuable for training. Together, these findings suggest that rather than minimizing stress, VR systems for public speaking should calibrate challenges to a productive zone and incorporate cognitive scaffolds that help users sustain performance under high-pressure interruptions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Prism-UX: Turning Evaluative Divergence into Traceable Design Evidence for LLM-Based Process-Level UX Evaluation.
abstract: Generative AI is increasingly being integrated into interactive workflows, introducing new challenges for UX evaluation because user experience is becoming more context-dependent and more closely tied to process-level moments such as waiting, flicker, uncertainty, intermediate artifacts, and loss of control. However, existing AI-assisted evaluation methods often compress such process-level differences into a single decontextualized conclusion. Interviews with 10 practitioners revealed that reviewers often struggle to cite specific moments in an interaction, compare interpretations across stakeholders, or trace their judgments back to observable facts. We refer to this loss of perspective-specific evaluative distinctions as insight collapse. To address this problem, we propose Prism-UX, a traceable review system for short, visually observable UI workflows involving GenAI features. Prism-UX first transforms interaction screen recordings into citable storyboard evidence through a frame-difference algorithm, then supports side-by-side evaluation from configurable evaluative viewpoints over shared evidence, and finally applies a structured reasoning protocol that anchors review judgments in explicit Fact IDs. Through a technical ablation study and expert evaluation, Prism-UX reduced the logical conflict rate by 84%, increased grounding completeness from 0.38 to 0.82, and was rated more useful than automated baselines for trade-off inspection, discussion support, and decision confidence. The results suggest that preserving evidence-grounded evaluative disagreement, rather than forcing convergence, can support more traceable and disagreement-aware design review.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Sketch, Edit, Flatten: Bridging the Gap in Fashion Design.
abstract: Translating a creative vision into a tangible garment traditionally requires technical designers to interpret a fashion designer’s 2D concept sketches into functional 3D mockups and 2D patterns. We propose a novel workflow that empowers fashion designers to generate 3D simulated garments directly from their 2D sketches. Our interface supports multi-stage refinement through a trio of tools: a Sketching tool for drafting ideas on an avatar’s front and back views, a 3D Pen tool for manipulating complex curve networks in 3D space, and a Flattening tool that converts enclosed areas into 2D patterns. By automatically consolidating 2D strokes into a cohesive 3D geometry, the system bridges the gap between conceptual drawing and technical simulation. Evaluations with professional designers indicate the system is both intuitive and effective, allowing for the creation of 3D garment shapes and patterns without specialized technical or pattern-making expertise.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Ptolemy: A Semantic Map of Exploratory Data Analysis.
abstract: A central challenge in exploratory data analysis (EDA) is keeping track of what has already been examined in order to decide what to analyze next. In practice, analysts often run dozens of analyses while building an understanding of a dataset. However, most tools provide little support for maintaining an overview of this evolving process, instead exposing only a linear history of analysis steps. These tools show sequence, what came before, but not position, how a current analysis relates to the broader space of possible analyses. As a result, analysts must mentally reconstruct which parts of the space they have explored and where gaps remain, increasing the risk of redundant work or overlooked patterns. We present Ptolemy, a navigational interface that externalizes analysis history as a semantic map. Each analytic step is represented as a point positioned by embeddings derived from a structured description of its effective data view (e.g., columns, filters, transformations), allowing spatial distance to reflect analytic similarity. In a mixed-methods study comparing map, canvas, and tree representations, we find that maps improve global orientation and local comparison, while ordered layouts reduce decision cost. These findings surface a trade-off between orientation and actionability, and highlight design principles for supporting strategic exploration in EDA.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Spray and Etch: Personal Fabrication of High-Resolution Electroluminescent Displays.
abstract: We present Spray and Etch, a novel personal fabrication method for bespoke-shaped high-resolution displays through alternating spraying of electroluminescent materials and laser etching. Personal fabrication of custom shaped displays has opened the door to fully free-form interactive devices. However, developments have been limited to low-resolution segmented displays, monochromatic output and methods that are prohibitively complicated for non-specialists. Spray and Etch combines low-cost deposition methods (airbrushing) and the use of common makerspace infrastructure (laser etching) to address these limitations, enabling high-resolution displays through easy-to-use methods. We contribute eight performance characterisations of this process and demonstrate its potential with a functioning passive matrix display that can dynamically display images and video. We show that Spray and Etch has the potential to be expanded to both non-planar topographies and dynamic multicolour displays. Improvements in resolution and usability through Spray and Etch represent a step change in the personal fabrication of free-form displays.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SketchMind: Toward Executable Pen-Based Sketching for Constructing Sorting Algorithms.
abstract: Pen-and-paper tracing is commonly used to think through algorithms before writing code, allowing learners to step through concrete executions and explore possible solutions. However, this process does not readily support abstraction. As traces grow, they lose structure. Steps accumulate into long sequences and are often skipped or compressed, leading to incomplete or inconsistent reasoning. As a result, learners struggle to extract reusable algorithmic patterns or generalize beyond individual instances. We present SketchMind, a proof-of-concept sketch-based programming system in which users construct executable traces of sorting algorithms through pen-based interactions. By performing operations directly on visual representations (e.g., arrays and variables) using pen strokes, users can construct and refine sorting algorithms without writing code. SketchMind supports four key capabilities: (1) executable tracing, where actions are recorded and replayed as runnable steps; (2) reusable pens, which encapsulate trace segments into user-defined procedures; (3) multi-level trace views across values, indices, and symbolic parameters; and (4) cross-instance validation, which applies learned procedures to new inputs and generates minimal counterexamples.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: BridgeScope: An Interactive System for Retrieving, Diagnosing, and Steering Cross-Modal SAE Features in Multimodal Large Models.
abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have become a key tool for mechanistic interpretability via decomposing complex model representations into human-readable concepts. However, existing SAE analysis workflows focus mostly on language models. In multimodal settings, a major question remains: are SAE-based concepts shared across text and image modalities, or are they specific to each modality? In this paper, we present BridgeScope, an interactive system for retrieving, diagnosing, and validating cross-modal SAE features in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). BridgeScope integrates three capabilities: (1) input-driven feature retrieval that identifies features specifically activated by text, image, or joint input while filtering out globally frequent features; (2) multi-dimensional cross-modal diagnosis that evaluates features along cross-modal embedding similarity, modality balance, intra-modal coherence, and semantic similarity; and (3) steering-oriented intervention that enables users to manipulate features and examine both intended output changes and unintended side effects. Through quantitative evaluation, case studies, and a user study, we show that BridgeScope helps discover shared cross-modal features, diagnose their cross-modal properties, and support targeted interventions in MLLMs.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Less Is More: Balancing Positive and Negative Space in Visual Concept Blending.
abstract: Graphic designers often blend visual concepts to communicate multiple ideas within a single image, leveraging positive and negative space to create balance, emphasis, and aesthetic appeal. While computational methods have begun to support automatic concept blending, they largely overlook the role of spatial composition in the design. To address this gap, we present an automatic pipeline that explicitly applies positive and negative space throughout the blending process. Our approach first identifies plausible regions for concept integration by combining semantic reasoning from vision–language models with geometric constraints derived from real-world examples. Conditioned on these regions, the system generates blended compositions using a hybrid pixel–vector pipeline: diffusion-based inpainting produces a fast, coarse initialization, which is then refined through vector-based optimization at the point level to ensure structural coherence and balanced semantic expression. A multimodal agent orchestrates this process as a planner and evaluator, enabling iterative improvement and interpretable control. Through an evaluation using both baseline comparisons and a user study, we demonstrate greater expressiveness, creativity, and concept recognizability by effectively leveraging positive and negative space. We further demonstrate the generalizability of our approach across diverse applications, including controllable image and infographic generation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: FleetScape: A Mixed Reality Sandtable for Spatial Supervision and Control of Scalable Drone Fleets.
abstract: As autonomous drone deployments scale from individual units to coordinated swarms, the human operator’s role shifts from direct piloting to high-level supervision. Current interfaces often treat multi-drone control as a scaled-up version of single-drone operation. We instead investigate how reframing fleet supervision as spatial interaction can better support the spatial, temporal, and safety demands of complex missions. We present FleetScape, a Mixed Reality (MR) sandtable system that externalizes layered real-time mission, safety, and environmental data while enabling fluid transitions between manual intervention and autonomous supervision. We developed a high-fidelity building inspection simulation that generates and streams synchronized multi-drone and environmental data for MR visualizations. We used this prototype to conduct a user study with six experienced drone pilots managing fleets of up to 15 drones. Our findings show that FleetScape supports situational awareness through layered spatial representations and clarifies control mode transitions. However, a limit to situational awareness was observed as fleet size increases, leading to different supervisory strategies. Finally, we derive design implications for supporting scalable drone fleet supervision.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: When and Where You Nudge Matters: Multi-Step Interface Interventions Against Address Poisoning in Crypto Wallets.
abstract: Crypto wallets are the primary applications through which users interact with Web3 ecosystems, and are subject to a range of attacks that lead to serious security consequences. Address poisoning is a prominent example: attackers exploit wallets’ truncated address displays and users’ habitual reliance on simplified transfer workflows to trick them into sending funds to fraudulent addresses. While prior work has quantified the prevalence and financial impact of such attacks, little is known about how to effectively defend against them. In this work, we take wallet interface design as a practical defense vector, introducing nudge interventions that help users resist these deceptions. This approach can be deployed through wallet updates without modifying underlying blockchain protocols, and directly targets the interaction point where the attack takes effect. We design nudges targeting three key stages of the transfer workflow where users are most vulnerable to this interface-induced threat. Through a between-subjects online experiment (n = 351) and semi-structured interviews (n = 20), we show that nudges can significantly reduce susceptibility to address poisoning attacks, but that their effectiveness varies depending on where and how they are placed within the transfer flow. Our findings offer design implications for building safer wallet interfaces, demonstrating how the placement and framing of interactive elements within a transaction workflow can meaningfully shape users’ security-critical decisions.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Sonic Stage: Automatically Generating Interactive Spatial Soundscapes to Facilitate Dialogue Video Comprehension for Blind Viewers.
abstract: Audio description (AD) makes film and television accessible to blind and low-vision (BLV) audiences by narrating characters’ actions. However, in scenes with lots of dialogue, AD often omits important actions because it is constrained not to overlap with speech. It is not yet known how to convey characters’ actions during dialogue. We present Sonic Stage, a system that transforms dialogue videos into interactive spatial soundscapes, enabling BLV audiences to intuitively understand characters’ actions and movements through immersive auditory cues. Sonic Stage conveys essential visual information during dialogue through three auditory techniques: (1) spatialized dialogue to represent spatial layout, (2) diegetic sound to convey character actions, and (3) interactive descriptions to provide context-specific visual details. Evaluation with 12 BLV viewers showed that Sonic Stage significantly improved video comprehension, spatial presence, and narrative engagement. We highlight opportunities for enhancing video accessibility across diverse genres through immersive, interactive audio representations.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: RemiAssist: A Therapist-Supporting System for Photo-Based Reminiscence Therapy in Dementia Care.
abstract: Despite growing interest in applying AI to photo-based reminiscence therapy (PRT) for people with dementia (PwD), existing systems primarily focus on PwD-AI interaction and often overlook therapists’ critical role in practical PRT delivery. We present RemiAssist, a system that supports therapist-in-the-loop PRT through AI-assisted planning and real-time facilitation. RemiAssist incorporates two core techniques: (1) a Memory Graph, which organizes key life events from a PwD’s photo collection into a hierarchical graph to support theme-centered intervention planning; and (2) a Context-Aware Guiding Strategy, which provides real-time suggestions to help therapists guide reminiscence conversations and respond to sensitive situations. A field study with eight therapist–PwD dyads suggests that RemiAssist was associated with a 44% improvement in planning efficiency, a 54% increase in conversation duration, and timely support for handling sensitive situations. We highlight opportunities for AI systems to empower therapists and enable more personalized reminiscence therapy in dementia care.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Programming by Teaching: Authoring Agent Workflows through Voice Conversation.
abstract: Agent workflow automation is increasingly accessible to users without programming experience, but much of the knowledge needed to author workflows is implicit. Programming by Demonstration captures what users do on screen but not the rules behind their actions. We propose Programming by Teaching, where users teach a task to an AI through real-time voice conversation while navigating the application, as they would teach a colleague. The AI listens, takes notes, and generates an agent workflow. We implemented both modes in the same Chrome extension and compared them in a within-subjects study with 28 participants, primarily non-programmers. Teaching passed held-out edge-case tests at 87.2% compared to 46.7% for demonstration (p =.002). Teaching reduced cognitive load (p =.04), scored higher on both pragmatic and hedonic quality (p ≤.001), and made it easier to incorporate rules not visible in the UI (p =.003). The hardest part of demonstration was not building the workflow but editing it afterward; teaching sidesteps this by front-loading specification into conversation.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: SnapAxis: Axis Based Interaction for Object Manipulation in Mixed Reality.
abstract: Accurate 3D object manipulation in mixed reality remains difficult when targets are distant or partially occluded. Existing techniques often improve local stages such as target acquisition or fine adjustment, but pay less attention to maintaining a stable and interpretable manipulation reference across acquisition, placement, and refinement. This forces users to repeatedly reinterpret control mappings, increasing cognitive load and reducing refinement stability. We present SnapAxis, an Axis based Interaction framework for MR object manipulation through smartphone. SnapAxis is organized around the Semantic Axis Handle, a shared object centered reference that links acquisition, placement, and refinement. The framework consists of three stages: ZoomCapture for target acquisition, Coarse Manipulation for Semantic Axis Handle establishment, and Fine Manipulation for continued refinement around the established reference. A within subject user study showed that SnapAxis significantly improved task efficiency and 3D alignment accuracy while reducing phone movement, head view search burden, and subjective workload.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Beyond Dense Sensing: Biomechanically-Guided Hand Pose Reconstruction from Reduced Observations.
abstract: Accurate full-hand dynamic capture in XR remains challenging because existing approaches largely depend on dense and layout-specific observations, including optical keypoints and high-density wearable sensing. Although such dense inputs can provide rich motion evidence under favorable conditions, they also introduce important practical limitations. Vision-based tracking becomes unreliable under self-occlusion, tool manipulation, and challenging illumination, while dense gloves increase hardware burden and often require reconstruction models tightly coupled to a specific sensing layout. As a result, existing hand-pose reconstruction pipelines remain strongly dependent on increasingly dense input observations. In this paper, we present PIRO-Pose, a biomechanically-guided sensing-model co-design framework for full-hand pose reconstruction from sparse wearable measurements. Instead of directly mapping sensor signals to poses, PIRO-Pose first transforms heterogeneous sensing inputs into a canonical anatomy-anchored sparse representation, where sensor reduction is guided by hand kinematic topology and inter-joint dependencies. Based on this structured representation, PIRO-Pose reconstructs dense hand articulation through anatomically structured graph expansion, multi-scale temporal modeling, and kinematic decoding with physiological constraints. Experiments show that PIRO-Pose achieves accurate real-time reconstruction on our in-house sparse-sensing dataset, remains competitive on a public high-density glove benchmark after compressing the original dense sensor streams into the same reduced interface, and maintains robust continuous tracking under severe visual degradation. Together, these results show that reliable full-hand reconstruction can be achieved not only through dense sensing itself, but also through structured reduction and reconstruction on a normalized sparse observation space.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: MemCanvas: A Structured Memory Canvas for Evolving Intent Alignment in LLM Dialogues.
abstract: Aligning user intent in complex, evolving dialogues with Large Language Models (LLMs) is a significant challenge. We attribute this to a cognitive divergence between LLM’s linear reasoning based on context and statistical semantic representations, and the exploratory, non-linear, and personalized nature of human intent. These gaps not only cause progressive misalignment but also leave users without a clear understanding of model’s perception or means to control its trajectory. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemCanvas, an interactive system that organizes dialogue history into shared, editable memory structures to complement outcome-based approaches. By scaffolding intent via three interaction primitives—Trees (for thematic directions), Relations (for logical connections), and Tags (for personalized semantics)—MemCanvas enables users to externalize evolving intent and proactively steer the LLM’s reasoning. Our technical evaluation and user study (N=28) demonstrate that MemCanvas effectively aligns user intent and enhances users’ sense of control, transparency and collaboration. Ultimately, this work illustrates how intent scaffolding can serve as a practical supplement to standard linear interfaces, fostering more process-aligned human-AI collaboration.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: RegulAR: Graph-Grounded Error Recognition and Assistance for Procedural Tasks in AR.
abstract: Errors are inevitable in procedural tasks, yet most AR guidance systems focus on step-by-step instruction delivery rather than helping users recognize and recover from mistakes. We present RegulAR, an AR task assistant for procedural error recognition and recovery. RegulAR models task instructions as a hierarchical dependency graph and combines this structure with a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) to interpret egocentric observations during execution. This enables RegulAR to track progress, identify deviations by error type, estimate their impact on later steps, and deliver appropriately salient interventions through an in-situ head-up display that visualizes task state and recovery guidance. By making procedural structure explicit, RegulAR supports not only next-step guidance, but also reasoning about what went wrong, why it matters, and how users can get back on track. In a within-subject study (N = 12), participants reported better task-structure understanding and recovery support with RegulAR than the MLLM-only baseline.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Cellery: Gradual, Composable Structure for Spreadsheets.
abstract: Structure in spreadsheets is typically restricted to ranges of cells and flat tables. However, replacing the open-ended two-dimensional grid with a more structured alternative risks limiting users’ freedom and impeding exploratory workflows. How can we enable expressive structure in spreadsheets while preserving their flexibility? We propose a model that allows users to gradually add structure on top of the traditional grid. To identify common structural patterns, we conducted a content analysis of 30 real-world spreadsheets. Based on our findings, we developed Cellery, a novel spreadsheet system that makes these structures explicit. In Cellery, users gradually define the structure of their spreadsheets using named groupings of cells, composing together four structural primitives: Atoms, Lists, Tables, and Blocks. Once defined, users can directly manipulate structures, dynamically reference them in formulas, and incorporate them in reusable abstractions. We evaluate Cellery with an expressiveness study reproducing spreadsheets from our sample, demonstrating that it is capable of representing types of structure that traditional spreadsheets cannot. In a preliminary user study of five participants, we find that they successfully use Cellery to design spreadsheets with explicit structure, and we uncover opportunities for further work on the formula language.
conference_title: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology

title: Surprise2Refine: Axis-Centered Exploration-To-Refinement for Agent-Assisted Creative Scaffolding.
abstract: Designers require different design spaces across creative stages: broad during exploration, and targeted during refinement. Yet existing agent-driven tools assume a fixed or continuously expanding space, leaving designers to manage and navigate it themselves. Informed by a formative study with five designers, we propose an axis-centered workflow that adaptively broadens and narrows the design space to support structured exploration and refinement. We implemented this workflow in Surprise2Refine, a prototype that allows users to build and reshape an n×n design space through a set of axis-centered interactions as their creative intent evolves.
